To be brutally honest here, I know why many people gave this game a bad review. Although, in general, I wouldn't necessarily listen to what most people said about the bad reviews. Although a fair portion of it might be true, it's more-or-less extremely exaggerated, and for most of the given part, is taken with a little pinch of salt. Is this game "Pay to Win?". I can't lie here and say no, but saying yes would be just as much of a lie. You can easily play this game without spending a single dime and actually be able to compete with other players. For me, I have 56-58 permanent characters (none are under 15$), and I would say I paid for less than 5-10 of them. We're at the point where complaining about a game like this being "pay to win" isn't actually a legitimate argument.
There are tons (when I say tons, I mean tons) of events that give away free crap all the time. Most of them don't really even require effort, it's just that people don't bother doing them. At higher ranks, you can argue that this game is competitive to a level that it's utterly boring, but there are ways to go around that. Do you need to play with the highest ranked players? Hell no, grab a friend and do a 1v1, and play for freaking fun. My main concern is that everyone is fanatic over winning that they've become corrupted, psychologically insane and some may even be lunatics. But it's easy enough to avoid these kinds of players: every single damn game has these guys. There's a block button you know.
To address concerns that other people have been complaining about, I first must put this out for the public to realize: THIS VERSION IS MADE FOR THE NORTH AMERICAN SERVERS. DO NOT POST BAD REVIEWS IF YOU CAN'T ACCESS THE GAME BECAUSE YOU LIVE SOMEWHERE OFF THE COAST OF BRASIL OR INDONESIA. I swear, half the bad reviews were just foreign people unable to access this game's version. Yes, lag can also be a slight issue, but if you live on the Eastern coast of North America you should be fine. Only some people experience lag from the West coast. As for bugs/issues, this game does have quite a few, but they're nothing game-changing at all. I mean, slight text bugs? Unreleased styles? Unintended prizes? If you're going to complain about SUCH minor issues, don't even bother to play video games in the first place. Period. Go grab a book if you get that startled over such little things. Most bugs aren't big, but it may look like an issue, considering this game has quite a few.
Although the purpose of this post was to tackle the certain complaints, if I were to conclude, I would say it's a great fighting game. Whenever I'm bored of playing shooters, action games, MOBAs or whatever it may be, I often find myself having a few matches on this game. Huge variety, uncomparable customization options, various modes and styles: it has all that's on my hit-list. Although it may not be everyone's cup of tea, but if you're into cartoony/animated (or anime) inspired visuals, along with a huge variety and great action, then this game would be for you.

A story is being told during the game in a native tongue and has captions for you to read so you can understand. However, you do not have time to read them as you flee a persuer and whilst performing precision tasks. Completing levels does not give you the sense of completion as solving puzzles in most games do as the feeling is merely a sense of relief as the stress of the previous level has finally been overcome. You have few tools for overcoming challenges and you are constantly being hammered to use the same tools to solve the same obstacles the same way over and over again with any failure causing you to restart from checkpoint. It is a very difficult game and is not enjoyable for a casual gamer.

I always aspired to be an evil genius growing up, instead I grew up to be some lazy gamer who plays games about being an evil genius.

Hello, I am a player of Lost Saga since it first launched in North America at OGPlanet (OGP) in November 17, 2009. It has since moved to Smilegate West. I was one of the first people to log in the first few minutes it launched. I will not state my full IGN here, but I will say it has stayed the same these past 5-6 years.
This is my review of Lost Saga in its current state, after half a decade of experience with it.
- Many maps and game modes for a large variety of gameplay.
- Ability to switch to any class in your roster during battles in most game modes.
- Highly customizable classes, and dozens to choose from.
- Fun, easy to learn beat-em-up style gameplay.
- Overall very polished game mechanics.
- Good sound effects and music that match respective menus and game maps.
- Bugs and issues after almost every update that usually make the game dysfunctional.
- Server issues causing lag and delay even for players residing in North America, often leading to frustrating gameplay. As of the posting of this review, lag problems are particularly unforgiving to players residing in the west coast and southern United States.
- Extremely poor community. Forums are not very active and are un-moderated to the point of allowing trolls to post on them whenever they want. Players in-game usually have foul attitudes.
- Very low population, despite the many great things the game has to offer.
- In addition to low population, matches are difficult to find depending on the time of day you choose to play; this is mostly caused by the amount of non-battling farm rooms that are created.
- Very "Pay to Win". There is a huge gap in fairness, especially for newer players. Although with a lot of time put in (roughly a year or so of playing) one can obtain most of the things they want. There is however a clear advantage for those who choose to delve into the pricey microtransactions offered. It is possible for a player who has only played for a few weeks to have a better account than a player who has played for a few years, through microtransactions.
- A mode called Faction War Mode has become stunted by the low population. It is only used as a means of joining something called the Elite Tournament in-game which pits teams of 3 against each other for a grand prize. However this mode has also become tarnished by various disconnection issues which have occurred for weeks at a time. There is also an extremely low chance for newer players to win or even compete because the tournament is not entirely based on how well a team can play the game, but on how much stats and money a team has put into the game for the glaring advantages. The tournament essentially does not put everyone on the same playing field with equal opportunities.
- Many unique heroes/classes to choose from but only a handful that are worth using as a "main", which makes most classes obsolete.
Lost Saga is a great game, in fact one of the best games I have ever come across. With the right backing and a more positive community outlet, it would easily rival other more popular MMO titles in the Free-to-Play market. However, it has not withstood the test of time very well here in North America, and is steadily declining as the weeks go by.
Smilegate West is a good publisher, but Lost Saga is a very demanding game with a just as demanding community. The playerbase has shrunk dramatically over the years, and most veteran players like myself have already given up on the game despite spending over 5 years with it.
The imbalances in the game are being caused by the Korean developers (IO Entertainment) who continue to release unbalanced content, which eventually reaches the other servers. The way Lost Saga is being developed in its own home country is only further widening the gap between old and new players.
In its current state, I cannot recommend Lost Saga to anyone.

I've had so many hours of fun with this humourous game.  I bought it on disk a few years back.  I bought the Steam version so I wouldn't have to dig out the CD.
You control an Evil Genius and all that comes with her/him.  You build an underground base and equip it with defenses against the good guys who are after you.  It's a top down perspective so you can design your base in any shape you desire and be able to see all your minions working and playing.
The objective is simple but not so easy.  You must get so powerful that the world succumbs to your evilness.
The good guys have hundreds of agents they send to investigate your island base.  In addition they have Super Agents that pray on your minions and equipment.  Fortunately you can hire bad guys/gals to aid in your defense.
You have minions, which comprise Construction Workers, Technicians, Head Shrinkers and Soldiers.  Later in the game you will have Mercenaries, Scientists and yes, even Playboys at your command.
It's relatively a stress free game, almost. :)  To really enjoy it you'll have to manually adjust some values with Notepad.

35mm is an interesting game. Let me preface this review by saying that if you're the type of person to get bored easily with slow paced games, you're going to struggle with this one; at least until it gets started, but it's definitely worth persisting with if you're a lover of a great story with an AMAZING atmosphere.
I'm currently Let's Playing the entire game on my channel.
The first video in the series is linked here -
Whilst the visuals are notably dated and the gameplay mechanics very basic, the game's ability to immerse the player in its unique world is unbelievably effective. The ambient sounds of the wasteland around you seem to swallow you up whole and sweep you away in whirlwind of mystery and intrigue.
You assume the role of a character by the name of Petrovich, though little else (or nothing else) about him is revealed at the start of the game. You start off outside an abandoned shack with your travelling companion, who we also know nothing about, on a journey to a destination which is also unknown. Are you starting to see a trend here? The only thing we know is that we're in post-apocalyptic Russia following an outbreak that wiped out the entire country, and apparently much of the rest of the world.
What are we doing? Where are we going? Who are we? So many questions wanting answers.
Will you seek them out?
Cheers guys :)

This is...an odd game.
It's not nearly as polished as the screenshots or videos might lead you to think, and you can visually tell it wasn't made with the resources a bigger studio would have poured on it. Animations are a bit off, maps are a bit...simple and one directional, enemies are fairly dumb, voice acting a bit wooden, the main character so cheesy you might as well grate him over a plate of pasta.
However...the game shines despite all of these flaws. You are a sniper, and by jove, the game makes you feel like one as often as it can. Having to snipe people from across a huge plaza in a limited time frame, prioritising targets, snipe-dueling enemy snipers by trying to spot them before they spot you or put a bullet between your eyes, causing distractions, incapacitating rather than killing someone so they'll act as bait for someone else to come and help them and expose themselves to your sights, timing your shots to coincide with a PA announcement or a bomb explosion or whatever so the sound will be disguised and, yes, even thinking on your feet when spotted and having to move from vantage point to vantage point picking off enemies or even defending a singular spot by sniping enemies and vehicle fuel tank cap to cause explosions. These are things that the game does very well.
And it does them well because sniping feels like it takes more skill than it typically does in games: you don't just shoot at the middle of the crosshair. Your rifles feel more like high-velocity crossbows that have to compensate for gravity and potential target movement. Particularily impressive shots will reward you with a bullet-time view of the bullet travelling to your target and viewing the damage it inflicts on an x-rayed model of the enemy. Your character is not a bullet sponge, he's in fact a glass cannon: brittle, but deadly. The games shines when it embraces this, and suffers when it veers away from, which thankfully isn't very often.
It's all an illusion of course: it's not a very hard game. It does the illusion well though.
PSA: I can understand a f2p or an ostensibly multiplayer game peddling DLCs, other products or other paid services on its main menu, but the obnoxious splash screens urging me to buy Sniper Elite 3 and preorder Sniper Elite 4 on both booting the game and exiting it are for some reason really irritating.

Darkness 2 is a first person shooter with fantastic story elements, environments, sound and voice acting. The story of Darkness 2 pulls you in very quickly. The cut scenes are in first person, so you feel like you’re right there in the middle of everything. I truly did want to progress in the game because of how involved I got with the plot.
I will preface this review by saying I would
More on that later…
Let’s start with gameplay. Being able to control 2 guns and 2 deadly serpents attached at your shoulders at the same time makes for some killer combos and devastating enemy deaths. The game is very brutal with serpent deaths. Tearing off heads and ripping in half is just a taste. Being that the game is called Darkness, you need to stay in the shadows as the light will disable your serpents and make it difficult to see to fire on your enemies. This effect is truly disabling and you will not survive fighting in the light for long. You can collect various amounts of essence by killing enemies which you can trade in for various skills that will improve your character. There is a “skill reset” option so in case you find some skills are not good, you can reset everything for a small essence fee.
Graphics and environments are stylized and really nicely done. It’s a split between comic book and real looking graphics. It fits right in with the story.
Sound and voice acting are top notch. The Italian mob voices are fantastic and each character is unique. It was always a pleasure to hear dialogue back and forth between everyone. This game has a lot going on for in-game sound. It does get fairly noisy at times but that’s just an observation, not a complaint.
Controls…they take getting used to. I tried this game using a mouse and keyboard but I found myself struggling. Switching to a 360 controller instantly corrected everything BUT the learning curve is still moderate. Stick with it and it’ll eventually become pretty natural.
Stability and FPS are rock solid. Never crashed once on Windows 8.1 and got a solid 60fps throughout the game.
Many times during the game my view would become slightly blurry. Like the game forgot to reset back the focus. The simple fix when that happens was to take a screenshot. It fixed it instantly each time. It did get annoying as sometimes it would happen during intense battles and I’d have to take a second to reach the screenshot key.
+Graphics, environment, story, gameplay and sound are all very well done
+Solid 60fps
+Brutal enemy deaths
+Solid variety of enemies
+Slight replay value with new game +
+Vendetta missions
+Controls take getting used to (use 360 controller)
+Shouldn’t be so many unbreakable lights.
+Some erratic graphical glitches throughout the game. But didn’t take away from anything
+Combat can get somewhat boring
+Darkling and Darkness tips can be repetitive
Bottom line is that Darkness 2 is a good and seemingly underrated game.

So, first of, I like this game and really want it to succeed. However, I am a meanie bobeanie.
The game has multiple game modes; two. Survival and Sandbox. The two modes are virtually identical, in both you play as a dinosaur till you die, however, in one you have to unlock various dinosaurs one after another, most dinosaurs being pretty much identical to each other in all but a few numbers.
The game started out as a glorified asset flip chatroom using the models from the game "The Stomping Lands", however soon after the team, lead by the guy who is well known for such amazing titles as "Primal Carnages Dilophosaurus", started to turn into a proper game with a proper vision. By now they have probably even nailed down that vision.
All in all, the game has multiple problems. First of, the balance is horrendous. While I starved to death once (during my most recent attempt at survival), my usual cause of death was animals a tier above mine outrunning and then oneshot-killing me (This includes animals like Herrasaurus and Allosaurus, which; while I am certain wouldn´t have a hard time killing a Velociraptor and Avaceratops respectively, would at leat need to do a bit more than bite its butt once). The progression system, in terms of balance, is not like dealing with a sloped curve or even a mountain, it´s like jumping to wholy different metric units. Most players who are in survival mode usually just want to get to a certain dinosaur. Which isn´t that hard currently, however, there have been no less than two instances of the sandbox mode getting removed for testing, usually followed by a huge drop in player activity and a huge influx in all the future marketing experts spamming "Git gud", before going back to studying or talking with their many friends.
Since this is a multiplayer game, I will also adress the community. The community is full of condescending asshats (like me), immature children and weird people. I mean, do what you want, but if you want to watch dinosaurs have sex; just buy a breeding pair of canary birds. The community is quite toxic. I usually wouldn´t care; but in this case, we are handling an online game with no AI (did the store page mislead you? I was sure they took that out long ago...) you sort of depend on other players to play. You will often run into players guarding corpses, killing everything that comes near; teaming up with other players to form huge packs that, if you are lucky, will protect members who get attacked and shun non-members away; or, if you are unlucky, hunt the whole servers population down and kill every last person. Some people still do the latter on their own. The devellopers don´t really do anything against any of these, to the contrary, they seem to encourage infighting between members of their community both with their elitist attitude (think neckbeard atheists; except they don´t have a point) and more or less accidentally with subtle game design decissions.
Let´s get to that next. Game design (here: a probably incorrectly used term to describe mechanics, map design etc). Currently, the game design is horrible. Animals can starve to death within a few minutes. Foliage is everywhere, but barelly any of it is edible. For example, at one point, my Orodromeus nearly starved in the middle of a hecking jungle. On the maps I played, water is also quite rare. I only found one lake on the map I played on, as well as two smaller swamps. Other than that, I counted a total of three unique looking locations. Which didn´t help much, since one was a hidden cave and the other two were so close to each other that it hardly mattered. The map is huge and unless you somehow got ahold of a Quetzal, you will not see it all during one lifetime unless you stock up on food. And even if, don´t bother. There is a chance you could run into one of the overpowered higher tier creatures. Or break your leg. Or starve to death.
Overall ranking;
Overall Realism gets a 6/10. While the game is trying its best to have realistic mechanics, such as starving to death and breaking your leg, it seems way to punishing with these. For example, some animals starve to death in less than half an hour. However, all the models are detailed, same with the ground.
Accuracy in terms of animals gets a 3/10. While almost all of the Ornithopods and Sauropods are very good in terms of accuracy, especially more recent additions like Psittacosaurus, Avaceratops and Camarasaurus. The Theropods (and Herrerasaurus) however have quite a few problems. Out of the Coelurosaurs, only three have feathers (One formerly had some, but that model is not in use and had its problems anyways). Those three are Austroraptor (which still sports a scaly belly and head) and the two herbivores Gallimimus (who was underfeathered) and Therizinosaurus (who doesn´t feature the distinct feathers seen in Beipiaosaurus, however, has a rather interesting, albeit rather outlandish bushy anteater-esque tail). The other three are plucked and naked. As if that isn´t enough, one of them; Utahraptor, is grossly oversized (It should be around the size of, but slightly shorter than Austroraptor) and also otherwise doesn´t look like Utahraptor anatomy-wise; instead it is a straight up JP rip-off. However feathered variants (and better feathered variants) have been confirmed, so I am confirming that I will edit this to raise the games accuracy score once that happens (for the record, the games actuall accuracy score would currently be around 5-7/10, however it will obviously raise if they add more accuracy to it). Other than that, the anatomy of most Theropods is spot on. However, the game takes part in both the "colour me unsurprised" (copypasting the colour scheme of a random living animal onto an extinct one) and the "Digimon" (sticking random spikes on everything. Sure. These are iguana spikes. That does not mean you have to litter everything that is not an iguana or has a lifestyle even remotely similar to an iguana with them. Or crocodile armor, in case of the Spinosaurids.) trope. The game also features supersized "Strain" variants, which are so ridiculously overpowered that they wouldn´t fit in any game even attempting to balance between the tiers. Luckily, the Isle was develloped by "The Dilophosaurus guy", so they fit right in. Balance: 2/10.
The musical score is nice, but forgetable. 2/10, try adding more sound to it next time. It could make the waiting times less boring.
UI nice but not give enough; especially during progression, 3/ also all over place. Leaves out
The code care is good. Bugs usually get fixed faster than you would expect, albeit less fast than Steve would expect. Stop being impatient, Steve. 7/10.
The gameplay is boring most of the time. Sometimes you run into a Dinosaur. Then it´s usually very fun by comparision, even if you are just stalkering it from the distance. 4/10 please don´t restraining order.
Overall score: 27/60

Played this game with 2 friends, story mode on hard difficulty was definitely challenging, especially some of the boss fights require multiple attempts, forcing you to learn the patterns instead of just smashing buttons.
Some of the level design reminds me of Legend of Zelda, combat brought back memories of Secret of Mana and brutal (but fair) boss design could be compared to games like Ys.
The game has "grind" in its name so if you're a fan of hunting for items, it certainly has that aspect aswell. There's really no reason to grind if you don't feel like it. The grinding aspect works well though, the longer you stay in one area and the more enemies you kill, the faster they start spawning with some of them being stronger "elite" versions of normal enemies. So the difficulty starts ramping up and it can get pretty chaotic after a short while.
Lots of fun with friends, just be aware that it is early access - not all of the game zones or skills are implemented but the core gameplay and mechanics are solid already.
We've yet to finish the story mode and we haven't tried arcade mode yet. But I can already recommend it, atleast as a co-op game if you're fans of ARPGs.

First of all, i'm not really into Star Wars, I like the setting, movies and the games, but i don't really care for the continuity of the "Star Wars Universe". So the fact that the game's protagonist would be "too strong" doesn't bother me at all.
First the good things, it has a nice storyline which is visualized by good looking cutscenes. The port is actually pretty good, it runs on about anything, and besides the simple level design, it looks pretty good and the effects are nice, considering the age of the game. Controls are ported much better than the first title. And (in this case a pro) you can finish the game in under 6 hours (steam says 4.8 for me, but i don't believe that). So you're finished well before it gets too boring.
Besides all that, i think _as a game_ this title has very little to offer. Level design is as linear an uninspired as it can get. There are only 3 level designs, and even in these levels it's the same corridor over and over again. They didn't even bother to hide most of the "crystals" you aquire to upgrade your health and force bar.
Also lacking is the number of different types of enemies, and special animations. For larger enemies it's the same kill animation over and over. Hexen 2 came out in 1997 and was developed by Raven on Quake 1 engine. It's mostly a single-player FPS with RPG flavor. Well, the way that it was done back in the day, not about plots but about wandering around. And it can also be played in multiplayer, both competive and cooperative. Sadly, there is no expansion pack for it in Steam, Portal of Praevus, so it's just stand-alone Hexen 2.
Now, seeing how id handled this Steam release? You guessed it, no CD music! But on positive side, Hexen 2 actually had MIDI music in it as alternative. While I would recommend you to track down soundtrack or game CD, MIDI is still a fine.
It also lacks intro movie, so you have to watch that yourself on YouTube.
It also includes only OpenGL version of a game, there is no Software option.
Otherwise, it's also kinda fine. Not sure about widescreen. It handles some HUD graphics badly on higher resolution screens, like it doesn't stretch intermission graphic fully. And then, it also kept all the original game's bugs.
Boy, was that buggy. My first game-breaking bug was in the Aztec-like world, where it kept failing to load location that I visited previously properly, just erroring out. Had to restart progress there with use of console commands. And then in Egypt-like world solving clock puzzle correctly didn't open the door in another location, making it unsolvable. Yay "noclip" command. And in greece world it would randomly crash because fish would randomly try to do invalid behavior or something. I murdered them later.
So yea, just get Hammer of Thyrion engine port. It should fix most bugs while it doesn't change the way that game looks. So purist like me will be happy.
Oh, and since it's Quake 1 engine game, don't forget to input "+mlook" console command for mouseview!
As for Multiplayer, well, it probably should work. This game screams for Cooperative gameplay with friend, I think. Even though it's still more of single-player experience. But since it has no server browser and isn't Doom/Quake, then I take it that community is "dead". Didn't find server with people at least.
Story follows Dragon Riders saga, as you have to take on the biggest and meaniest red menace of them all. And so this time around you will have ot travel through few time periods as well, visiting dark castles, Egypt, Greece, Aztec. Hm. Well, actually you have to travel over four continents of Eidilon world. And well, just go and read the manual, find it in Internet. It's worth it.
Nothing much going on in the game though. Didn't bother with special music for intermission/ending even!
So, now about Hexen 2 itself. Great sequel. I actually think that it did a much better job than Hexen itself. The only thing that original has over this is a bit more colorful setting. Otherwise, Hexen 2 mostly improved and fixed some of the problems I had with original. It's more interesting and less repetetive.
One of the small changes, as you would expect, are classes and leveling. There are four of them now, but they all still dare to have only 4 weapons, which is shame. But now as classes level up, they will open two additional abilities. Most of which are actually pretty passive and wouldn't change your playstyle.
-Paladin is mostly focused on head-on meleeing, your first hub will be spent swaying only sword. His first ability is that he swims with same speed as running, while second ability is that he may regenerade instead of dieing. So, pretty passive stuff, but still fine character.
-Crusader is another head-on class, but not as focused on melee. His abilities are all focused on keeping himself alive. One ability is that he will randomly get health bonus while fighting, second ability is that enemies sometimes will drop Holy Power, to power you up for some time.
-Necromancer is slow character who is stronger at range. His first ability is that health may drop from enemies. Second ability is strange, you can sometimes get health by hitting enemies with melee attack. Seeing how he is slow and weak, it's pretty much not worth it even if you are lucky.
-Assassin is a weak direct damage output yet fast character. It's also supposedly stealth character. Character with freaking stealth abilities in a game where AI doesn't do anything to make them worth it! First ability is that she can become invinisble in darkness if she stands there for some time. Useless. And she can backstab enemies with her melee. Which is hard to pull off, at rare times when enemy isn't facing you. And even if backstab does few times more damage than usual melee hit, her puny melee weapon is so weak, it doesn't do anything good in the end. Just forget about abilities and concentrate on damage-avoiding playstyle.
This time your character will level up as you kill more and more monsters too. Leveling up increases stats like health and mana, but you will not get to choose what to do with level-up. It's just a little thing to make killing every enemy worth it. And thankfully, it's not Hexen 1.
When you compare Quake to Doom, you will notice that they focused on having less enemies in each encounter. Whether it is for the better ot not is not something easy to decide. And Hexen 2, running on Quake engine, has much less enemies per encounter than Hexen, running on Doom engine. And boy, this one is actually much more fun in this case. Combat in Hexen 1 felt too repetetive, having to kill dozen dumb monsters with 4 weapons for whole game. Hexen 2 improved it by focusing on less yet smarter or just more interesting enemies. Hexen 1 would swarm you with annoying shielding centaurs, who just dumbly walk twoard you and shield for few seconds upon any damage. Hexen 2 has shielding were-jaguars, who actively jump, run and roll around, only sometimes putting on shields, with the game throwing only around 2-3 of these dangerous tough enemies at you in same time.
Not only that, but Quake engine allowed puzzles to get much more varied. Hexen 1 was about finding switches to find more switches. Hexen 2 will make you run and wander around, looking carefully at walls to see breakable ones, making you bring sand to the forge to turn it into glass or solving a time puzzle in Egypt. You can agrue that it's almost same by complexity, but it's much more interesting this way. Especially the first hub and Egypt ones, they are very mysterious. it also helps a lot that Hexen 2 is more detailed, having houses filled with furnite, for example, thus making exploration more interesting.
Sometimes it lacks enough clues though, making you wander around for awhile. Or finding out that some wall was actually passable like a ghost wall. That happens. That, and it's still much much more puzzling than what most FPS players ever expect. "Puzzling" as in "Where am I supposed to go next?".
Music is also pretty good. It's mostly remixed of Heretic and Hexen music made to sound more ambient. Has some good tracks of it's own.
And well, while I mostly like this game a lot, it has few annoying things. One of them is physics. Player control. For some reason it feels like they wanted to appeal to Quake speeders. Diagonal running is SO much faster than just running forward, it's very noticeable. And well, I don't usually like such weird controls. But well, it's for some reason is quite addictive, as in few hours I ended up strafejumping up the slopes at high speed as a way to move between location.
Well, okay, that wasn't so bad, what is actually bad are pools of water where walls aren't lowe enough. In these cases you have to gain actual speed when you reach the surface, you have to shoot yourself out instead of just climbing out, pretty much. Too challenging. Don't forget to bind "swim up" in controls.
Also, ocassional unavoidable damage bring game down.
Hexen 2 improves a lot on Hexen ideas, not being as repetitive and more fun. While you may be frustrated while playing it, once you are done, you will remember this adventure fondly.

Story
After a severe car accident, Simon Jarrett suffers from severe brain damage, searching for medical help he agrees to an undergo experimental procedure. Simon has an unexpected blackout during the procedure and wakes up inside PATHOS-II, an underwater station tucked deep below the Atlantic Ocean. With no idea how he ended up there, Simon searches for answers and a way to return to home. Encountering enemies, nuetral forces, and friendly assistance, Simon uncovers memories of the past and terrors for what the future may hold.
A story about purpose, identity, and human life, Soma is breath of fresh air in terms of storytelling.
Gameplay
I don't mean this to pose as a con (it's worth noting)  but the controls themselves are shallow in terms of interaction with the world around you (more on this later). Typically a click of the mouse or click-and-drag mechanics are the extent of your capabilities, with a few exceptions where picking up and throwing objects is useful. Player and object/enemy animations are satisfactory and realistic. The enemy forces you meet inside the stations and while roaming the ocean floor come across life-like, and while their behavior is rather dumb at times, they still pose a challenge in certain instances.
Accurately believable physics and player movement build a sense of immersion. Chapter length and atmospheric variety set a nice pace that is both haunting and beautiful through out.
Sound
Incredible. Soma has arguably some of the best sound effects I've heard in a game. Every action no matter how minor feels like it was given careful planning in regards to how it would sound. Large metal airlock doors, compartments de-pressurising, pulling a levers and accessing control panels, a strong current flowing through a tunnel, all masterfully created to build a fuller experience for the player. All accompanied with sincere and emotional dialogue that is as engaging as it is thought-provoking. The characters you meet feel alive through their emotion fueled ideas, pleas, and thoughts.
Graphics
Beautiful. Paired with just as wonderful audio, Soma's graphics exceeded my expectations and the attention to enviromental detail is remarkable. Every room and corridor contain visually pleasing detail and their structural design gives the impression that they may actually exist.
Lighting and visual effects are as masterfully crafted as they are unsettling. Leaving the confines of the stations and roaming the ocean floor is about as eerie as you would expect while still maintaining an atmospheric beauty that makes you want to explore. Hands down an incredible experience visually.
Replay Value
What took about nine hours to complete with few instances of dragging, I would argue that though their is certainly a lot to discover, but there's not much worth going back for. Soma provides a compelling story that is unique and thought-provoking, but at the end it conveys what it wants the player to see and understand and closes the curtains.
Wrapping Up
I personally wouldn't quite peg Soma as a horror to those looking for a good scare but it is certainly suspenseful and unnerving.  As previously mentioned the controls themselves and interactions with the world around are shallow in complexity, but the combination of story, sounds, and graphics provide a truly wonderful experience. Incredible game overall, a must play.

FIRST IMPRESSIONS:
I.
Poured the gas into a railroad cart. It's somewhat reminiscent of Metro, but instead of shooting radioactive mutants, I'm shooting pictures with my 35mm camera. And no, it's nothing like Pokemon Snap. However, for a game I had little to no expectations of, I can say I'm pleasantly surprised and constantly catch myself thinking that it's pretty decent for being developed by a single person.
And now I'm off the cart and into a new area that can only be described as quintessentially "russian", my friend whose name I have yet to hear marches onward towards our first encounter with other humans. This is where they introduce game mechanics similar to Telltale Game's Walking Dead series, e.g. timers and button mashing. It's obviously not there to create a challenge, rather it serves as an instrument to the game's atmosphere, narrative, stream of consciousness, or whatever you want to call it.
Something that I keep encountering when I'm playing this game, or in one example, while I was on a short little mission to fill up a bucket of water outside in the dark, is a sense of dread that's not unlike that of a horror game. But what makes this unique over any of those games is that there's this prevailing sense of dread in certain moments, and it's mostly derived from I think is fear of the unknown. Everything about the game is mysterious, from its Russian origin, the shoddy translation, slow paced gameplay, it's all so silently overwhelming. And that's incredibly clever. I think that sums up what this game is to me. It's clever and it's obviously the summation of many hours of love and diligence that only a one man production effort can possibly accomplish. It's not polished, it's doesn't make your eyes pop out, at least not yet. But it's a GAME, whatever that means, and it's interesting and original, despite being yet another post-apocalypse game.

To be honest, if I were to give this game an honest review, I would say that this game receives a medium rating. However, there is no option for that on steam, so here we go. For Honor is a "realistic" fighting simulator giving you immersive gameplay with an innovative fighting style.
Starting off, here are some pros:
It's great to play with friends! It's fun to fight the enemy team with your friends either on or against your faction, or you could just play brawls privately and 1v1 till your hearts content.
It's looks. The game looks great. It's true. Even though I don't have that great of a computer, the game runs really nicely and looks beautiful.
Some Cons:
Balance. This ones obvious if you've read other reviews. You could pay 100$ to get a metric tonne of steel and buff all of your gear to max level and destroy every enemy you come across on the battlefield. Also, almost every game either me or my friends are always complaining that a certain class is overpowered.
Stale Gameplay is another con that I feel not that many people mention, however I feel as if it is very apparent. Almost every fight you initiate the same way, do the same combos, and then either one of two things happen most of the time: either you kill them like a complete god, or they get scared and cheese you by throwing you off a cliff.
Rewards. The reward system is complete garbage. At Reputation 29, all you get is a pretty lame pattern that looks like the one you just got at the beginning of the game. It does not feel that satisfying.
In conlusion, the game receives a 7/10 in my rating, because For Honor is really fun to play with friends, however the gameplay will eventually get stale and not very rewarding.

Like some of the reviewers here, I started this game when it was hosted at OGPlanet during 2009. I played for about three years, so please don't be fooled by time I put in steam for this game (although I also did spent considerable time here as well). Overall, during OGPlanet time, I spent about $500 on this game, so you can tell how much I have invested in and how much I liked.
But I cannot recommend to anyone here on Steam to play this game. I will skip usual bread and butter review. Here are the reasons why you should not waste your time (and money) on this game. If you can get past these reasons, then be my guest, download now and enjoy the brawl.
1 - Player base is shrinking. It is harder to find a
game room as your level higher. The game also have skill level system. Which means that you are doing well (Kill/Death ratio), even though your player level is let's say level 1 (they have military style ranking), the game will only find you game room on higher level than level 1 because, well, your skill level is now higher than level 1. Which can give you many problem. You have lesser room to play. You will face higher level player (although not that bad).
2 - Farm, Farm everywhere! What is farm? Well, as you guess it, there are some events going on and most event are based on how long you log in to game and how long you play particular game mode. Sound cool, right? Yes, but the problem is again with player base. I don't understand why these players do what they do. You will not find game room where players are actively, well, playing. They make game room, instead of playing, they just sit there until, fight time counter runs zero. The point of this game is all about fighting and brawling but right now all games are like that. If you don't farm (stay idle), game room host will vote to kick you out. If you just leave your hero idle, the game itself will kick you out for AFK. So in the end, you join a game room to fight but instead you just run around nothing to do. Does that sound fun to you? Not to me.
3 - Game is very latency sensitive. Unless you stay very close to server, you will not get the good ping. Not like other online games like DOTA or LOL, here lag is very visible. Because all your input needs to happen in split second, and if you are lag, the other player suffer! Yes! it's the other way around. Lag wins you. So why does this bad? Well, imagine you lag horribly, you input a punch, it register to another player 10 seconds later. During that time, the other player might have been furiously pressing his punch key to you 100 times but never hit you. He won't be happy, you also won't because all you see is delay after delay. Fighting game with lag is horrible experience.
4 - No strategy, no skill, just spam to win. Although, the game promote creative way to fight each other, here is the a simple truth which has been true since the game come out. Just spam the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of attack to win. There are some considerable hero that are mostly hated but really just for spamming. One of the example is 'Cyborg' hero, who can just stand behind and spam your attack grenade launchers. Another hero is called 'Gangster' (used to be Mafia back in the days), just spam the gun shooting. Although, there are many ways to counter and win these heroes, in reality, the game is very broken to the point that it is not fun anymore.
5 - The higher the level, the more toxic players you will encounter. Although, this is not just new to online gaming, especially I know in DOTA or LOL, you will find many hostile players, the community in Lost Saga is in a way very
. If you are older player like me, you will find it annoying or irratitated to the point that you just block the chat to really play the game in peace.
Summary
----------
- Shriking player base.
- No game room, Farm everywhere
- Lag means no fun, and the service does not seem to be better in future
- Spam to win
- Bad community. A lot of 12 years old
Don't play this game.

Never Alone is an educational puzzle platformer about a native Alaskan girl and a white fox that saves her from a polar bear. The game play centers around using each of the characters' abilities to proceed further in the level and supports local co-op. The story is a teling of an old native story, comprising different elements of the culture in question. The game I'm most reminded of is Brothers: a Tale of two Sons. The two-part puzzle solving draws a lot of parallels, but is designed for two people to play. The story is nice and told in the native language of the people; unfortunatly if you don't speak native Alaskan, you'll have to read the subtitles. The game is short (about 3-4 hours). If you like documentaries, there is about 30 minutes of native Alaskan people talking about their culture, which is enlightening.
I can recommend this game with a couple of stipulations: the first is that I would suggest watching each unlockable part of the documentary after each level. It will provide a good pace and won't break flow. The second and most important is that you should grab a friend to play the co-op with. unlike Brothers, this game's play style was designed for two people to work together, and even though you can switch between the two characters, several portions of the early game and most of the late game requires them to act near simultaneously, which can make the game play sticky and frusterating if you are playing by yourself.

In general, this game is DEFINITELY worth a buy when a sale comes out or if you're a big fan of horror games and especially Friday the 13th, it's very true to the films.
People complain that Jason is OP, he is meant to be, Jason always wins one way or the other, you're meant to die most of the time, it's just a shame a few cheap tricks can be used by Jason to make your games last about 2 minutes some of the time, such as a Jason who only grabs, or uses his ability to close the distance for an instant grab.
I wouldn't mind a bit more variation in kills too, both environmental and grab-based, there's a good few but not as many as there could be. I'd also add that Jason should be able to pick up weapons he finds as he did many times in the films, sometimes I fancy using a machete, other times I fancy using a pitchfork, doing this would open up many more grab kills as well.
The game needs a bit of a polish, the launch was terrible for Xbox One and PS4 players, PC players only suffered at the start.
As mentioned earlier, the players are also a bit tedious. I rarely get a full lobby, especially when I am Jason because 2-3 players leave, solely because they are not Jason, they've essentially bought the game for only half of its value, to play as Jason.
I'd give this game a 7/10, above average, but it will easily earn a 10/10 in the next 3-4 months when more stuff has been fixed and added into the game.
People need to stop griefing the devs, they have no knowledge of what they're dealing with, they have a small team, and an even smaller one to deal with the problems encountered on launch, they didn't deserve the hate they got from arrogant people claiming they deserved the game AND a refund, you bought the game with faith that you would enjoy it, and you will, but these errors are bound to pop up one way or another.

- Jason.. looks... awesome.  Music is on point when he coming too but could use some change up
- Perks and outfits add nice variation (when they work - currently broken or aren't completely negated by Jason)
- There's some fun transitions to be had with the car and battling for it with a group.   However, the boat is lackluster.  If Jason catches you in the boat - you're done.
Cons
- not much feedback from the UI (you dont know weapon stats, status/durability, equipped perks or how they affect you)
- no single player / skirmish / offline mode (but singler player is coming)
- no way to set custom controller / keybinds
- No audible noise for the boat when its starting so it's hard to watch for Jason or other counselors (the car makes noise when being started)

He would at least cover ground quicker to help and start with an inventory full of items to help support (first aid, firecrackers and a pocket knife for example). Let me begin with this: this game is definitely not your average shooter. It will certainly feel like it at first, but be prepared for a game brimming with subtle art and literature references .
The Darkness II plays and feels almost like the controls found in the Bioshock series, but with a neat twist...You can use both demon-tentacle-head melee attacks and dual-wield pistols simultaneously. I honestly haven't had this much fun since classic Shadow Warrior and Rise of the Triad. It has a pretty unique visual style that borders between actual comic book and cel animation.  Digital Extreme's in-house Evolution Engine is extremely well optimized and the use of light (and darkness) and shadows are second to none. To be honest, I was not impressed by Jackie Estacado and his entire crime family. I very nearly stopped playing the game. They were all run-of-the-mill and BASIC ♥♥♥♥♥es. Once you discover that this is simply a delusional fantasy of a man at a sanatorium , things begin to become interesting. The attention to detail in this game is another aspect that I enjoyed thoroughly: The radio in the room. The phone conversations people have that give details about the story and make you wonder if you're insane. The really neat Lovecraft short film in the rec room. The paintings. My Ravioli's Too Spicy! (Pay attention to this, it's a hilarious overlap) The Darkness is a metaphor for mental illness and I'm pretty sure that this illness is hereditary as there are references to his father attempting to find a cure for the darkness for himself and his boy. In closing, the transition and overlap between real-life and fantasy is very well implemented, and in my opinion was the most interesting part of the game. The ending was sort of ridiculous, but all of the other positive aspects definitely made up for it.

From the creators of S.T.A.L.K.E.R, what could be a better reccomendation? Unfortunately the final result is not that great, Survarium as in version 0.30 is a rather disappointing F2P fps shooter, at least given the high expectations raised from the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. legacy.
Pros:
- Nicely drawn and detailed maps, one playing differently than the other.
- Anomalies provide a new feature compared to standard shooters.
- Realistic gun sounds and effects.
- Four different fractions to choose with different weapon / equipment settings.
Cons:
- Few maps, gameplay tends to get repetitive after some spending some hours
- Battles seem to be very unbalanced both in tier ratings and in player efficiencies.
- A lot of "pay to gain advantage" elements, they ruin game progress: Ok, it is reasonable to expect premium account, or premium equipment to advance faster (like War Thunder or WoT). But here besides these you are almost forced to pay gold to modify equipment, to buy extra maps for after-battle looting etc. This is too much, it creates a gap between paying and non-paying players. For example why to have just a 50% probability of success to modify something when you pay with "regular" credits (and parts) and 100% probability when paying with gold? Not to mention that I seriously doubt if the 50% rate is accurate...
- Small-sized teams lead to serious balance issues when players from one side disconnect or go afk.
- Seems to be a very large fraction of players with hacks. This is very serious, actions should be taken to prevent cheating rather than punishing it. It simply ruins the experience.
- Small player base, at late times balanced battles (with respect to equipment) seem to be the exception.
- Anomalies and the related environment seem greatly undeveloped. An aspect which should be central to a S.T.A.L.K.E.R-based game. Their visual effects seem controversial, personally I would prefer a different implementation. Benefits and dangers from interacting with anomalies, which are very localized and small-sized are also under-developed.
- way too much spawn killing.
At this point I can not recommend the game. Perhaps in a future update I will revisit it, especially waiting the free-to-explore-world mode. As it stands now it has potential, but the general gaming experience is underwhelming...

Knowing Frictional’s past series (Penumbra and Amnesia, which I highly recommend checking if you’re into this genre) and always wondering how such a small team can put so much value into their games, I knew from the start that SOMA would exceed my expectations. And so it did without a doubt!
Starting with the atmosphere, I can easily say that the developer did a great job in creating a legit, ‘realistic’ setting filled with few, but believable, characters that drive the remarkably intriguing story. The environment is extremely detailed and well-though, filled with notes, audio logs and other objects, which really adds to the immersion. The underwater sections are, simply put, astonishing – approaching different sections of Pathos-II from the outside, the facility in which the game takes place, felt almost real from the outside. The story presents a really though-provoking concept, does a great job at it and manages to keep you interested throughout the whole game – I wish more games would approach such subjects. Combined with the horror aspects of the game, you never really feel comfortable, on the one hand because of the infested environments and on the other hand because of the tense encounters that you get into from time to time, which can become repetitive later on.
However, one thing I must point out and that is the sound design. It’s just so immersive – I would really like to see a version of SOMA made for Virtual Reality. That would be a hell of a ride for sure! The amount of depth and spatiality that each sound has is incredible and I personally haven’t seen a game that manages to do so well regarding sound, which, in my point of view, is a must, especially for horror games. It has that real-life authenticity which can be easily heard when the protagonist speaks, when there is a monster in a room nearby or when crawling through vents and things happen anywhere near you. (There’s an article the developers wrote regarding the audio, so you should definitely check it out if you’re curious!)
Performance-wise, the game ran pretty good, with generally constant frame rates. However, there were some hiccups here and there, usually when loading a new map and when going inside (from the underwater parts) and the textures could’ve been a bit better for a 2015 game, but there’s nothing game-breaking to worry about.
It’s kind of sad to see such high value games being made by teams as small as Frictional’s and not getting the recognition that they deserve, sometimes being ever better than some AAA games out there. I definitely recommend this title for horror/story-driven games enthusiasts and I’m really looking forward to seeing what the developers have to offer next.

I've been a fan of Hexen and Hexen II since my youth. I decided I'd give this game another shot and ultimately, I still think it's a pretty good game in general. It's fun to explore and the fact each classes have different weapons gives the game some replay value. Most of the puzzles in the game are reasonable although they get a little harder later in the game. The game has some pretty good music but as far as I know, it doesn't have files for CD music so it means you might be stuck with Midi. The first attempt to clear the game might take a pretty good amount of time as well so for a first person adventure game, it's length is pretty reasonable.
However, this is a game I'd only recommend to people who aren't impatient. There's a fair share of exploration required to do and at times and some of the puzzles can be rather frustrating or some hints can be somewhat unclear. At some point, areas might open to continue progression but it's not always perfectly clear where you're supposed to go next. The last few worlds are particularly bad in that regard but I wouldn't say it ever gets unfair. On the other hand, I'd say Hexen did a better job in general to figure out what has to be done or at least, the exploration doesn't get as tedious.
Still, anyone who's willing to explore the game and have the patience to understand the puzzles will most likely have a fun experience. Some of the areas are actually memorable with how they've been designed and I'd say the maps gets even more fun to visit as the game progresses.

To be honest, if I were to give this game an honest review, I would say that this game receives a medium rating. However, there is no option for that on steam, so here we go. For Honor is a "realistic" fighting simulator giving you immersive gameplay with an innovative fighting style.
Starting off, here are some pros:
It's great to play with friends! It's fun to fight the enemy team with your friends either on or against your faction, or you could just play brawls privately and 1v1 till your hearts content.
It's looks. The game looks great. It's true. Even though I don't have that great of a computer, the game runs really nicely and looks beautiful.
Some Cons:
Balance. This ones obvious if you've read other reviews. You could pay 100$ to get a metric tonne of steel and buff all of your gear to max level and destroy every enemy you come across on the battlefield. Also, almost every game either me or my friends are always complaining that a certain class is overpowered.
Stale Gameplay is another con that I feel not that many people mention, however I feel as if it is very apparent. Almost every fight you initiate the same way, do the same combos, and then either one of two things happen most of the time: either you kill them like a complete god, or they get scared and cheese you by throwing you off a cliff.
Rewards. The reward system is complete garbage. At Reputation 29, all you get is a pretty lame pattern that looks like the one you just got at the beginning of the game. It does not feel that satisfying.
In conlusion, the game receives a 7/10 in my rating, because For Honor is really fun to play with friends, however the gameplay will eventually get stale and not very rewarding.

Now lets take an honest look at this game.  I have a little bit of a bias because I have invested a lot of time and money into this game since it came out.  However, that's just the thing.  I have spent money on this game.  Lost Saga and it's players have a VERY heavy pay-to-win mentality.  Now, while having exclusive content isn't always a bad thing in video games, especially free ones, this game (just like every free asian mmo) shows you all the cool things that you can get that can help you but you'll be forced to play the game and get in-game money in order to extend the time limit on the heroes you have.  This can become tedious and set you down a path in which you'll realize that it'd be better to spend money on getting a character without the time limit.  Another thing is the gears.  There are many gears in the game and they can be easily be purchased with in-game currency, however, for a new player who has very little experience with the game, collecting 48k GP is going to be a real struggle.  While you don't need these gears to win, but if you want to make your characters look more appealing as well as have the skills of other characters to help you in battle, you're gonna want to get these gears.
Now, the big thing about this game that makes me tell people that they should avoid it is the community itself.  In my honest opinion, after playing this game since OGP days, it is absolute garbage.  You can't go a minute without seeing someone calling someone out for losing or showing their frustration by rage quitting or something.  It's sad to see that the game's community has not gotten any better.  Trash talk is so common, it makes me mad for all the wrong reasons.  Not because it's rude or anything, but because of how frequent I see it.  Also, if your connection is anything but perfect and you lag, players will relentlessly chew you out for that.
This concludes my Lost Saga review.  Overall, I enjoy the game and enjoy it enough so that I felt like pouring my money into it, but if someone were to ask if they should start playing it, I'd tell them no or that the many mixed reviews this game has already received are all completely justified.

Note: This review is written from the perspective who played the game SINGLE PLAYER, not co-op. I'm willing to bet co-op (which is LOCAL ONLY) is much more engaging in some aspects.
So when I received Never Alone as a gift, I was ecstatic. It looked like a heart-warming, investing tale involving a little girl and her fox, with some puzzle-platforming elements to keep the pace intriguing. Thing is, while that's definitely what I got, I'm still having trouble completely recommending this game to most people.
For one thing, the game is quite short. I'd be shocked if even most achievement hunters spent more than 3 hours on this platformer, and for a $15 price tag? That's asking a lot. The story, while heart touching, is quite simple and can really be summarized in a few sentences. The puzzles aren't tremendously difficult, though a few did keep me scratching my head for a minute or two. Where the game really seems to fall short are the bugs and the horrid AI you get when you're on single player. The companion you're not actively playing seems almost determined to jump off cliffs or to screw up the progress you make in a puzzle, and I lost count of the number of times I'd make a jump only for a sudden gust of wind to either stop or kick up and kill me.
So why give this game a recommendation? It's really a mix of the heartwarming tale, the beautiful environments, and the incredible attention to detail with describing Inuit culture and beliefs. The intent of the game and how purely it seeks to achieve that is admirable and really deserves to be watched. If I had to recommend to someone whether to buy Call of Duty DLC or this game, I'd definitely say this. I'd rather the market be steeped with educational and emotionally investing material, even if this game didn't entirely satisfy me. If it's on sale, I say buy it, and maybe get a friend to tag along beside you.

Being a massive Friday the 13th fan (the original Paramount 1-8), this game is a dream come true. I never thought that there would be a day that the movies got another game, but the second I found out about the Kickstarter and that it was possible, I donated and kept up with the games progress as often as I could. I am not disappointed in any way with the game, even with some bugs/glitches at the moment. This is truly a game for the fans, by the fans. With that said, $40 is nothing if you love Friday the 13th and have been waiting for something like this. I know most fans backed the game during the kickstarter and paid more than that, as did I, and I would do it again in a heartbeat. If you aren't a die hard fan, yes, I could see where $40 is too much considering the amount of content in the game at the moment. The only thing I could say to counter that is from what I know, the developers will continue to be adding content to the game overtime, some/most of which will be free additions (like single player & a bot mode). Maybe down the road if more content is added and you still are interested in the game, you may consider the $40 to be a better bargin at that time.
The music by Harry Manfredini couldn't be better. It truly helps put you in the Friday the 13th world, and make you feel like you are possibly part of one of the movies. It is one of the best aspects of the game to me, and they 100% did it perfectly. The main thing that I love about horror movies in general is the atmosphere, and I think they did an extremely good job of recreating the feeling of the movies here.
There is a nice laid back fun feel to the game, where "winning" isn't the entire point of the game, at least to me. Simply managing to survive as long as possible and knowing that you are helping your teammates by at least distracting Jason is very rewarding. If you know what you are doing it is also very possible to get away from Jason, and even escape on a quite regular basis. At the moment I have a decently higher rate of escape than I do being killed, but I am aware that may change as people become much better at playing as Jason. With that said, I prefer to play as a counslor. It seems most people prefer to play as Jason, to each their own. I like the hide and seek dread that you feel as a counslor, and knowing that if Jason finds you, you will have a very tough fight on your hands. Even if you aren't able to escape and survive (win), managing to get away from Jason and trick him at some point in a match, just to be able to survive a few more minutes is very rewarding.
Theres a lot more I could say, but I'm sure its all been said before in other reviews here. If the game seems like it may be fun to you, try it out, its an absolute blast. If you like the idea of some extreme hide and seek, you'll love it. Yes there have been bugs, but the developers are working on them, and I'm confident they will continue to do what they can to help the community.

What you see here is a rather niche game, an early RPG hybrid space RTS, it is immensely fun, and while it can involve a lot of saving it scratches an itch in space game fans.  I've not found another game that really does what this game does, the starpoint Gemini games come close but not quite like this one.

Looks wise it can be similar to the Homeworld games in many respects, especially with the engine trails that allow you to track fighters easier.  Imagine if instead of a massive fleet like you have in Homeworld you had a carrier, and your heroes commanded the fighters.
There are a myriad of fighter classes to choose from, ranging from interceptor classes to heavy fighters and advanced supports vessels, all of which you can equip your heroes with, each having a different hull and the ability to take different classes or numbers of weapons, all of which you can pick.  Weapons range from light fast firing machineguns, heavy cannons and lasers all the way to missiles, then there are systems you can equip that improve the crafts performance.
Even your mothership can be fitted with various weapon in a range of calibres, plus, making a debut in this game, heavy calibre capital class guns specifically for firing on opposing motherships.
Heroes can also be customised with various skills that can range from piloting skills that enable them to dodge incoming fire, gunnery and missile skills that let them hit impossible shots, and system skills that give them blanket benefits for the squad or debuffs for the enemy.
Some even have unique skills to handle certain ships and weapons, or even call in on-the-spot reinforcements to help you in a jam.
All in all while the dialogue may go on a bit (plus there is little voice acting), the looks still hold up, the gameplay (while punishing at times) is solid once you get the hang of it, and the cuntomisation and freedom in the game is well worth a look when it's on sale.

Nether is a game by devolpers who are tired of the zombie genre, and want something more terrifying to stalk gamers as they trek through the dense city of whatever its called. scavenging for food and first aid kits to heal your wounds from the teleporting, shrieking, and demon like nether creatures. They are a force to be reckoned with and should be avoided at all costs.
Supplies are limited but not hard to find either. I can promise you that you'll come across a pistol in a matter of minutes, with enough ammo to get yourself out of a jam on your way to a safezone. Along the way, you'll find all sorts of different types of ammo, food, first aid kits, and lots and lots of junk. This junk however is used to be sold to the global market for cash which will in turn be used to buy supplies (ammo, food, aid kits) after a couple of trips through the city, you'll soon enough be making so much money, you'll always have enough ammo and supplies. At this point you can start participating in the dynamic events that unfold at the safezones I.E. nether attacks. But this got old after awhile really fast.
at this point, i had played about 2 hours, fully stocked on ammo, food, more than enough guns to take on an army, and the nether creatures became less and less of a threat. At which point i got bored and stopped there. However most people who play this game right now, become so power hungry, with an intense desire to show their power. and what a better person to show it to, than a lowly new player with nothing but a kitchen knife.
The community behind this game is quickly shrinking, (something like 120 players)  leaving behind the players who are determined to break the game and just wage war on every other person, because they are bored. If you are new, you will be shot. If you are nice, you will be shot. if you avoid people, you will get shot. if you leave the safezone, you will be shot.
TLDR:
This game had such an interesting premise, the creatures are fantastic, The area is dense and full of secrets, and surviving your first hour is heart pounding. The one huge aspect of the game however bogs down this marvelous experience, and that is the lack of a decent community. Want a more polished game like DayZ? this might be for you... that is if you like stalking other players while they struggle to survive, and then shoot them in the face because you're bored, then this is the game for you jerks!! Otherwise give this game a pass.

The total amount of time it took me to play through the game is as you see. 5 whole hours.
Now normally I would be pretty irritated with a game only having 5 hours worth of gameplay. It's pretty absurd, even for a shooter with some RPG mechanics. However, I purchased this game for 80% off, so it was a steal on my end, and 5 hours for a game that was less than $10 (far less if I recall), isn't really all that bad of a deal.
On to the meat of things.
The game graphics are pretty good, nothing spectacular, but even after 8 years they still had their appeal. The game is extremely graphic for kill moves and blood/gore, so if you're a gorehound you shouldn't be surprised as a basic mechanic in the game is ripping out hearts and eating them.
The big thing for me in this was the gameplay though. It's fast and furious and never lets up. The tentacle controls are fluid as are the handling of the weapons in the game and both are easy to grasp and quick to master. The difficulty of the game isn't broken (which is always a plus) and even when you die you don't have to repeat massive chunks of the game over again (which is also a plus).
Story...well...okay so here's the thing. The story is kinda blah, not bad, just blah. Sure it has its moments, and anytime Jackie gets to sit in the dark smokey room and talk for a bit I'm all ears, but it's still blah, or rather, generic if you will. This game follows the aftermath of the first Darkness, of which I only played through the tutorial. I was sidetracked with other games at the time and just overlooked it, so it never got the playtime it deserved.
The story compared to the comics is pretty spot on. Power wise, probably not so much as the comic version is pretty much godlike, and while in this game you're no push-over, you're not a god either. But hey, that's where the fun comes in. There is enough progression using their power trees to allow you to be awesome with guns, awesome with the Darkness, or handy with both. Of course the game offers you the option to continue playing after the story is over using the "newgame+" feature which will make you feel like the powerhouse everyone claims you to be should you go back and play this game sometime down the road.
The ending to the story was a bit of a let down, and somewhat silly, and featured some re-skinned models of baddies. But that's pretty much the whole game. No real enemy variety combat wise until you're 70% done with the game, and everything is just a re-skin of the same basic model. It's a shooter, so I don't expect much, but I do expect demons to be a little different from the mobsters in the game and not just a re-skin of the mobster and his gun. I played this game a lot when it came out. I must say it was a hit back then and I was rooted to my 15-inch monitor salivating profusely to the awesomness this game offered. Lush, colorful graphics, great gameplay, cool puzzles and unique weaponry made this game my favourite entertainment of 1998. Then by some terrible accident  I stomped on my CD with copy of this game and didn't finished it.
So 14 years later I spottted this game on steam an thought I would give it another try,
It didn't age well. If You think about all possible nightmares of retro gaming this one has it all. Hard as hell and unforgiving in a wrong way. I can still play first Quake/Doom/DN3D without feeling cheated but this game seems to be very imbalanced. It is known for it's notorious puzzles which are very frustrating and irritating. Opponents feels sometimes awfully overpowered, especially bosses. Colors and overall graphic design seems bleak and desolate which might be intentional back then but today it just feels empty and unappealing. Apart from that overall perfomance seems to be quite choppy on lower resolutions (the way it meant ot be played by the way). If You boost the resolution up with unofficial mods it works fine but levels looks very simple and raw because texture show their age. You may think that I might be spoiled with recent AAA titles but for me it's just not that fun to play anymore.
I still kinda like it for nostalgia reasons but I just can't recommend it anymore.

ROF has been my favourite dog-fight game/simulator for the last 5 years. Glad they gave the option to migrate to Steam.
Single player is available but it is mostly a multiplayer game.
Epic dogfights with aircraft from the WW1 era.
If you are new to this game. take your time to fine tune the controls and learn to fly the free aircraft properly and set up your joystick buttons and keyboard assignments.
Most important bits: 3 axis joystick. yes you WILL need your rudder with these flying contraptions.
If you have more than 1 hardware throttle lever, setup the second lever for mixture, third for radiator etc.
you can save the joystick setup per aircraft so don't worry about future multi-engine aircraft.
Joystick buttons: Elevator pitch trim up/down, Fire gunns, reload/unjam guns
Keyboard: I have assigned my head position forward, aft left right with the arrow keys. A huge disadvantage of a bi-plane is that the upper wing is in your view. the ability to quickly move your head is a game changer in a dogfight. Many people use it with TrackIR, I don't because I don't like how it works, maybe I need a bigger monitor for it.
Enjoy the most of this game by setting all the realism settings to hard, and learn that pointing the sharp end of your bullets towards your enemy (how ever difficult that is!) is not nearly the most challenging aspect of a WW1 dogfight.
For the pilots amongst us, adverse yaw, P-effect, Gyro-effect, dynamic and parasite drag). all of them are modeled in quite a good fasion. Good piloting skills makes a difference!
Once you master the free aircraft, or if you have a favorite aircraft, spend a few bucks/pounds/moneys on it. it's well worth it but not required to play the game.
Hope you enjoy the game! feel free to contact me if you want a chat about this game or aviation in general.

If you buy here on steam, you cant use the original online shop and vice versa. Or so i have been told.
Available career starting dates depend if you have the historical correct plane available for that time window.
If you buy a dlc you get maybe one or two planes that you want and need for your carreer and two or more that you did not want, but paid for anyway.
Just as an example:
German carreer from 1916:
The most interesting plane to start with would be:
Fokker IIIE --> You need the Birth of warbirds DLC
After just 3 weeks in career the Fokker is obsolete and you want the:
Albatros DII --> You need the Bloody April DLC
Which is followed by the:
Albatros DIII --> You need the Furious Wings DLC
If you want to obtain later on the most powerful engine for the Fokker D.VII:
Fokker D.VIIF --> You need the Ultimately the Best Fighter DLC
You see. To play the german carreer from beginning to end, you will probably buy 4 DLC's. You can work around some of the dlc's by choosing less powerful or popular planes. But anyway, it would be way more customer friendly if you could buy one dlc with all the planes from one country.
But still. My verdict is that this game offers tons and tons of content and a superb flight feeling for a reasonable price! The planes and dlcs go regularly on sale and large junks of the carreer can be played with the planes that are for free. So there is no excuse. Hop in and give it a try.

SOMA has several weaknesses - the puzzles found in the game not only are rare but also disappointingly easy for something that calls itself a horror adventure, the monsters tend to be more annoying rather than horrifying, and you spend the better part of the game simply walking from A to B while the gamer sputters forth its narrative.
It is this narrative and the atmosphere created by it, however, that really make the game shine. What starts out as a more or less regular visit to a doctor quickly turns into a biomechanical underwater nightmare that repeatedly questions the philosophical concept of the self and what constitutes as a human, anyway.
Long story short, SOMA basically is a glorified walking simulator, but unlike most other games in that category, this title actually has a story engaging enough to let you forgive its rather lacking pure gameplay. Those looking for a pure horror game that constantly keeps your heart pounding may be disappointed, however.

In Rock of Ages 2: Bigger and Boulder, you play the role of a historical figure trying to bust down an opponent's castle by rolling a boulder through a level whilst protecting your own castle from your opponent's boulder by placing various obstacles in his path.
Rock of Ages 2: Bigger and Boulder is a fun mix of Rolling Ball and Tower Defense genres of games and is quite unique concept that is well-executed and is a blast to play with friends.
Pros
- Rolling the boulder and avoiding obstacles placed by your opponent feels good and is easy to learn but hard to master.
- Placing defenses to stop and slow down your opponent's boulder is fun and requires a good amount strategy and tactics.
- Choosing your loading consisting of a choice of boulders and defenses at the start of a match allows you to focus on certain strategies depending on the level and on countering your opponent's choices.
- So much content: 15 levels that are truly different in how they play and look, 16 different boulders (most of which have unique characteristics and/or abilities) and 19 different defenses.
- Humour is expressed through the visuals, the voice acting and the gameplay and it's quite funny.
- Game can be enjoyed with a friend through the entire campaign locally and has various different modes of play locally and online.
Cons
- Campaign might be a little too easy if you're playing against the AI and you're really good at life/games. I recommend playing against friends in 1v1 (local or online) or 2v2 (online) matches.
