Just some initial impressions while this is on a Christmas sale.
As you'll probably have gathered, this isn't a AAA title. So there's some rough edges to this, especially in the campaign overview parts of the game and in the smoothness of using the UI. What Slitherine do really well, however, is the tactical part of space combat. There are enough options to neither overwhelm with detail but still provide some choices which influence the battle. The WEGO system works really nicely, and the addition of the Z axis does make a difference to how things play out. Just darned fiddly to manipulate movement along it at times.
I'd like to see the campaign extended more into a larger more open-ended sandbox. The campaign map could also use some rethinking. It's a muddle at the moment which would look better done in a style similar to DoW2 or Battlefleet Gothic. Also wondering about the longevity of the campaign as you are playing one faction in it and there are finite choices to make to shift things up.
Despite those niggles, I think I would recommend this. Slitherine have said there's more to come so hopefully they'll come good with that. It certainly manages to capture the flavour of BSG, and that's no bad thing in itself.

ABOUT THIS GAME
Experience true combat gameplay in a massive military sandbox. Deploying a wide variety of single- and multiplayer content, over 20 vehicles and 40 weapons, and limitless opportunities for content creation, this is the PC’s premier military game. Authentic, diverse, open - Arma 3 sends you to war.
Key Features in Arma 3
Altis & Stratis
Defeat your enemy on a richly detailed, open-world battlefield – stretching over 290 km² of Mediterranean island terrain. From expansive cities to rolling hills, whether steamrolling your tank across the dusty plains, flying a transport helicopter over the dense forests, or waging asymmetric warfare from the rocky hills, the islands of Altis and Stratis are dynamic worlds, which lend themselves to the most varied engagements in gaming.
Weapons & Vehicles
Head into combat on foot, drive armored vehicles, or take to the skies in helicopters and jets. Conduct a combined arms attack over air, land, and sea, with over 20 vehicles to drive and pilot, 40+ weapons to pick from, customizable loadouts with short- and long-distance attachments, and various types of gear to suit your needs on the battlefield. With a massive arsenal at your disposal, Arma 3 moves you into a world of tactical opportunities.
Singleplayer
Follow the story of Ben Kerry, a soldier who gets caught up in a Mediterranean flashpoint, across three gameplay-driven campaign episodes: Survive, Adapt, Win. Immerse yourself in Arma 3’s diverse gameplay by completing the focused showcase scenarios. Run through the competitive firing drills to hone your shooting and movement skills, and complete your training by signing up to Arma 3 Bootcamp, which features SP and MP tutorials, and a dedicated Virtual Reality practice environment.
Multiplayer
Fight online in the massive military sandbox that is Arma 3. Form a squad and team up against your enemy in the official Defend and Seize multiplayer scenarios. Or jump into one of the many popular unofficial game modes developed by the Arma 3 community. Experience a new form of multiplayer in Arma 3 Zeus, where Game Masters have the ability to influence the battlefield of other players in real-time.
Content Creation
Start creating your own experiences with Arma 3’s intuitive scenario editor and powerful modding tools. Enjoy a platform filled with player-created content, ranging from custom weapons and vehicles, to intense singleplayer scenarios and entirely new multiplayer game modes. Share and discover content on the Arma 3 Steam Workshop, which lets you install player-created content with a click of a button.

I used to like this game a lot and I saw tons of potential for an amazing game in it. It had a nice Community, and despite beeing unfinished the game was a lot of fun. Now the game just slowly digs its own grave, with lots of problems beeing ignored and a very close minded Playerbase.
The biggest Problems for me at this point are how the game itself plays out though. The game takes too long, the way the progression system works in this game is not functional. It takes you hours on hours to just progress to the next tier, you barely have any advantages of it and it feels more like you're beeing punished for playing the game then beeing rewarded for trying to unlock the next tier. Despite the system being broken in the first place, it is also incredibly hard to get around in the game. The map is gigantic, which makes it hard to find food, other players or genereally anything that isn't grass or water. The game does have its hot spots, like lakes and small forests, but in most cases those are blocked off by groups of people that will protect it against anyone that is not part of their group, giving other players no chance to survive. Which brings me to the next problem. It can take you up to 20 hours to unlock the last tier. If you die, you loose everything. No backup, no save, you just have to start as a weak little dinosaur again.
There are so many problems with this game, the devs and the playerbase that I completely lost the will to even open this game up to see if something changed. The game seems to progress itself into its own doom, which is a shame because I honestly wish it could live up to it's potential it once had. At this point it's hard to see the positives about this game, and if I'm honest, the only positive thing about The Isle for me are the Dinosaur models.
I really wish this game is going to catch itself and progress to the better, but I doubt it's going to happen. Don't buy it until some serious changes will happen.

The ultimate "Quantity over Quality" shmup, and the quality is still pretty damn high.
This isn't the type of shmup with 5 levels with the ultimate goal of 1CC'ing it. However, it does feature the traditional Arcade (Another Chronicle) mode with Darius branching paths, up to 10 different final zones.
This is a shmup with a "console" vibe to it, trying real hard to justify it's pricetag, and I was surprised when the pricetag is insanely justified.
The Chronicle Saviors mode isn't designed around beating a few levels without using a continue and that's it. It has a worldmap where you start at Level 1, or "Scenario" 1 would be a better term for this. When you beat Scenario 1, you go on to the next Scenario, sometime there's multiple paths. Think kind of like Super Mario World map, but without the pretty landscape. These Scenarios aren't just a level or just a boss fight, it's a set of levels and boss fights of various lengths. Some are short with 2 levels+2boss fights, some are long with up to 17 total levels+bosses. A scenario like that alone offers more content than most shmups. I've unlocked nearly 90 scenarios so far and so far as I beat them, they're still unlocking more. These scenarios can be challenging because you can't use a continue within one.
Obviously, with so many scenarios and many of these being pretty long, you're going to come across recycled content. There isn't 100 levels and definitely not 100 bosses (but there sure is a lot, with varied forms). There's so many scenarios because of mix and matching levels+bosses, but also mixing what ship you play (there's about 8 ships), and changing how the level is played (some are about doing it fast, some starts you off with no power ups, some starts you off OP). It's the type of game you might not intend to see the end anytime soon, but will keep you occupied for a long time without feeling like a chore.
As I said earlier, there's a few unique ships that changes the way to play. One has no special ability, one has a big black hole, one has the kamehameha beam from G-Darius, 2 has a laser that can be used defensively, and another one has something weird and hard to explain. The stages and bosses were clearly designed to be played different based on which ship you picked and makes it feel very varied.
As for production values, the ships and bosses looks fantastic, but the background isn't particiularly interesting or excessive, often feels like it might as well be black. The music however is unreasonable amazing, composed by Zunata who has done the entire franchise, they created some amazing music that has great variety and very unique sounds. Speaking of which, many scenarios in Chronicle Saviours mode are based around nostalgia, and you'll hear music from the older Darius games while playing as that games ship too (no capture system for G-Darius ship though, still the cool laser beam though)
I have 20 hours so far in this game and I only beaten half the levels I unlocked, and I still didn't unlock all of them. The dual-monitor support is pretty awesome for a horizontal shmup, but it's only used in AC mode.

This game overall is pretty good, but at the same time, just leaves a bad taste in my mouth.
|PROS|
- Models, Skins, and Animations are beautifully crafted, this goes for the foliage as well.
- Progression is fun and innovating way to motivate you to not die.
- Great Map Size with the 100 player servers, which means you are less likely to be cramped into a tiny space.
- Separate servers, like how some are for Realistic game-play and some just to chill out with friends.
|CONS|
- Community is terrible. They blindly follow developers, without analyzing anything for themselves, and are also♥♥♥♥♥holes in games. For example, you could be chilling with friends along a lake, then a random Shantungosaurus runs up and mauls you. They really have no decency. Just watch how many maul this review for not agreeing with their opinions.
- Developers are immature. They scream for us to "Get a better PC" whenever we lag, and they really just screw around on random servers playing as a Human or a Hypo, and destroying anything for fun, or what they call "Testing".
- Dinosaurs can be glitchy. I mean, I get that it's early access, but its been over a year. I think it could be better. Some glitches include spawning outside or under the map, not being able to eat certain corpses after they die, and sometimes when you fall in a ditch, you are forced to die, which really gives no fun game-play value as you are forced to stand there until your hunger and/or thirst drops and kills you.
- V4. This is a personal opinion, but I really dislike V4. The map is very unorganized, and is basically a mish-mash of separate environments. The spawns are terrible, and you very rarely see an herbivore with the minuscule amount of blue ferns.

Most of the time you're forced to hide behind a rock or a tree, or risk losing your hours of work to a hungry Apex. I, along with many others, get bored trying to reach the top of the food-chain, especially as a Carnivore.
Though this does have plenty of potential, I really cannot recommend this game. If you haven't bought this game yet, I wouldn't recommend doing so. Wait for something more promising like Saurian to come up, which isn't too far away as this review was posted.

This is by far my favorite game of all time. BeamNG is an extremely advanced vehicle simulator. I love all of the incredible features and details. The crash physics are the best of any game ever made, and the engine thermal simulation is very good and realistic. There isn't tire wear simulation yet but I feel like it will be added eventually. The customization is very in depth and it's fun to mix and match parts. The creators are constantly improving and adding new features, and I hope the development of this game never ends. You can tell that the creators love this game and put tons of effort into making it as good as it can be. I hope they keep adding cars and features for years to come, I would have absolutely no problem buying dlc if it were to be released. I would buy this game ten times over because of the price and the amount of time I've gotten out of it.  The modding community is great, and a few creators make mods that you can't even tell apart from the base game.
I never get bored when playing BeamNG. There is so much you can do. Crashing, road racing, drag racing, off roading, drifting, rock crawling, pretty much anything that has to do with vehicles can be done in this game. As of right now, there is a decent selection of cars and maps in the base game, but they are adding more.
I play this game on an i7 6700k, 16GB RAM, GTX 970 and get really good performance, anywhere from 60-144 fps depending on the map and how many cars are spawned in. I use a combination of a keyboard, and a Thrustmaster TX wheel. The force feedback is good how it is now, but there does need to be some improvements made to compete with Assetto Corsa/iRacing. As of now, there is no split screen or online multiplayer, but there is multiseat. I don't mind not having multiplayer. I don't feel that it's needed.
Anyone and I mean ANYONE who likes cars and realistic physics MUST BUY THIS GAME. I can't recommend it enough.

Doom is a timeless classic that defined what first person games are all about.
The plot is fairly basic, with not much given to you, you fight an increasingly more difficult army of demons thanks to an experiment gone wrong on Deimos. The gameplay is pretty straighforward, you kill demons and advance to the exit of the level, sometimes collecting multiple keys along the way.
Doom is also well known for having secrets all over the place, including some sweet secrets that may help you skip some tough levels, if you're feeling lucky... The secrets are also sometimes difficult to find, but it wouldn't be a classic game without some thinking.
The difficulty also varies, the easiest setting makes enemies pushovers, and you typically fight the less difficult ones, while nightmare respawns enemies, you always fight the worst, and the game even warns you it is not even remotely fair, still fun though.
I strongly recommend this game for anyone, classic gamers, or people who are just looking for a fun, difficult, time consuming game that will sometimes really make you think, or in one level, outright troll you, please do buy it, id did an amazing job!

This game looks like it'd be really fun,  but in reality the developers have made some reallllly stupid choices.
First off,  the eliminate the NA Servers so everybody would have play on the EU servers.  Basically for NA players are you going to get farmed.  This game is unplayable at a 200ms ping.  Essentially there is ZERO prediction in this games net code.  So at 200ms even if you fire first in to the back side of an enemy they will turn around at the first hit and kill you before all of your bullets register.
So with the aforemention problem I go in to the second problem.  The Armor to Damage output of the weapons is completely out of whack.  This coupled with zero prediction means armored low ping enemies have all day to react to you.
Cash shop items.  They are really pointless in this game period.  Especially any guns or armor.  They cannot be upgraded period.  What makes them even more pointless is the matching making in this game.  It is done based on the level of your gear.  So if you think it would give you an advantage it doesn't because you'll end up taking this gear up against people who have upgraded heavely.  Essentially you are better off just playing through the game and collecting the currency you get through playing matches.  Which leads to gear you can upgrade.
Population.  The population is so bad in this game that you'll will sit around for 5 to 15 minutes waiting for a match to start.  That is by the way after all NA players were forced to play on EU servers.  So for a game with PvP only modes this just nails the coffin lid right on.
The Developers have promised a fix NA players.  The grand master plan?  Allow players to select which servers they want to play on.  Question,  Why not make this change first and totally not screw over your player base?   Because really this change is pointless.  Players will have the choice of low ping and a lot of extra time between matches and a high latency unplayable game.
The graphics,  This is actually the first game I've ever seen that actually looks worse when you go in to the higher graphics settings.
Another thing players should no about.  The client for this game allows seeding.  I'm not sure what you are actually seeding.  But what I can tell you is this game maintains an active internet connection after you shut it down.

SOMA is one of the most thought-provoking story-driven games I have ever played. The story itself is constructed very well and makes you wonder things about not only the game itself, but it even taps into reality as a human being.
The baseline of this game is that you are thrown into a post-apocalyptic world as some confused and terrified character named Simon, who simply went into the doctor's office for a brain scan; and something went wrong, naturally. You then traverse through the dangerous environment deep below the Atlantic, searching for answers as to what is going on in this hellish world. The fact that Simon is in just about the same position as you, the player, being clueless and feeling vulnerable, makes it all the more immersive. The rest of the story, I'd have to leave up to you to find out about, as most of this game is purely about figuring out what's going on in the PATHOS-II Facility.
The gameplay itself is very basic, where you only do a few things to interact with the environment. You can open/close doors, use your handy tool to unlock stuff, find banks of information to learn more about the world and what happened at PATHOS-II, and run in terror from horribly frightening monsters. The monsters, at their cores, are quite similar in that they will chase you down until you die, but I love the diversity of them. Once again I don't want to spoil much about them, but there are monsters which you'd rather see as opposed to another... The only way you can evade death from those frightening and corrupted creatures is by hiding, running, or outsmarting them. You get no weapons, no means of harming them, nothing, it's up to you to get out of the way of danger; that alone makes the game terrifying.
Overall, the atmosphere is incredibly immersive with its excellent sound and visual design. I only encountered about one visual bug throughout the entire game, but even then you'd have to basically search for that bug. The monsters sound creepy as hell, the eerie ambient noises of being deep below the surface in a deteriorating facility make you paranoid as all hell, and the sea life makes you want to never venture below the waves again, and just get back into that horribly claustrophobic monster-infested facility.
Pros
Cons
tl;dr This game is a masterpiece, and if you are into Sci-fi, you need this game. While it is a linear story and you don't get very many other things to do after you've completed the campaign, the story itself makes that worth the price for me, but may be pricy to others. As a bonus, there is fully functioning workshop capabilities where you can make your own stories, and play others'.
If you're into horror, it's a must-buy while it's on sale.

A fantastic example of a horror game that actually goes beyond what many smaller studios think is necessary of a horror game. Instead of relying on tired gameplay and tropes -- oh it's a dark house, and I only have a flashlight -- Soma explores something deeper, namely consciousness and the grey area that exists implanting human consciousness in artificial, man made technology. Set in an underwater compound, after a catastrophe that has potentially wiped out life on the surface, you're set with a task of preserving humanity however you can, in whatever medium possible.
Following up from Amnesia: Dark Descent, a solid game that saw a lot of attention and hype despite being fairly by-the-numbers was always going to be somewhat of a difficult task, but Soma succeeds by pushing out of that comfort zone and trying something brave and something new. Something that genuinely elicits thought.
All in all, an enthralling idea, world and concept, but widely similar gameplay to its predecessor. A very necessary purchase for any horror fan.

The battle mechanics of this game is quite compelling. The planning out of the manuvering and targetting of each ship requires a very strategic mind to overcome each matchup. The biggest factor that I like is that each ship has its armor divided into all 6 dimensions of the ship, forcing the player to monitor the ships positioning to extend its viability in each battle. Additionally, while the weapon choices are generally limited (guns and missles) each ship has such a design that it doesnt 'feel' limited in its scope
Another big factor is the ship designs, they feel very authentic and based in the lore of Battlestar Galactica, like they were all genuine cannon from the TV series. The only downgrade in regards to its visual aspect is that I feel the game could use a bit more refinment and enhansement, especially in the department where the ships could show battle damage (to indicate which hull sector is damaged or broken). This was a big design element in the BSG reboot and I feel it should trickle down here as well.
While the campaign story itself leaves something to be desired, the campaign mechanic is very well designed. Its not overwhelming, but the fact that you only have one "Base" and you have to guard 12 colonies over 4 star systems, it means the player has to plan out their build queue and fleet deployment very carefully so as to protect their income sources.
Aside from the two small dings I mentioned, the game is absolutely a good pick for any Battlestar Galactica fan, certainly the best that I've played to date. For other players, I do see non-fans having some difficulty getting into it, but I urge them to give it a fair go. Its mechanics are uncommon (at least from what I've played) but overall well balanced. Plus I hope for some its a launching pad for the player to get into the series

I'm going to state straight away that this is one of the very best shmups ever and one of the greatest games ever made. And, actually, I don't even think it's quite the best Darius game, so that says a lot about how awesome this series is as a whole. As it stands, however, this is the best shmup on all of Steam (yes, even better than Ikaruga and DoDonPachi), and it will be a tough game to topple in terms of future releases.
It's not simply because of the sheer mass of content the game has, which, even if it's repetitive and the aesthetics are not as colorful and trippy as previous Darius games, equates to being far larger than any other shmup on the market with stages reaching into the thousands. It's because of the game's mechanics. One might say it's easy to make a game where you move a ship and shoot at enemies moving on screen. Whether that is true or not, the real difficulty is making a shmup truly stand out from the pack, and that's a major reason I'm a fan of Darius in general is how the game flows as you progress, particularly the flow of the enemies (they're space fish with fish-like patterns). As per usual with Darius, you can select your own path in this game within the variety of game modes, and the difficulty rises about as appropriately as can be possible in a game such as this. It does become death-heavy somewhat often, but as with the other Darius games, it says a lot when I die and proceed to say, "I love this game."
As a huge fan of shmups and especially Darius, I purchased this one straight away and have been in awe ever since, and I've only scratched the surface in terms of content I've delved through. This is one of my very highest recommendations on all of Steam. If the price seems steep, I can assure you it isn't, though I'll understand if you wait for a sale. But even at full price this game is more than well worth the money.

"Dariusburst" is a horizontal shoot'em up that was born initially in PSP (Playstation Portable) in 2009 and was later ported to arcade receiving expanded and improved versions ["Dariusburst: Another Chronicle", arcade (2010) and "Dariusburst: Another Chronicle EX", arcade (2011)] until finally this last version: "Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours" aka "Dariusburts CS" release in 2015 for Playstation 4, PSP Vita and PC Steam. One of the most remarkable and peculiar characteristics of the Darius series are the enemies, especially the bosses who are all fish or aquatic creatures. Another feature is its "sui generis" soundtrack, developed by famous Zuntata, band formed by employees of Taito Corporation. I can say that "DariusBurst CS" is more an excellent addition to the series, bringing three main modes: AC (Another Chronicle) Mode, a direct port of "Dariusburst: Another Chronicle EX";  CS (Chronicle Saviours) Mode, impressively rich in content, with a lot of different stages (186 stages in total) and varied missions and routes that can be chosen, making the game quite high in longevity and finally a DLC Mode, where you can purchase new ships and new types of gameplay. Now talking about the game's features, the graphic style adopted is beautiful, running in high definition with great fluency, the controls are accurate and work very well (I used the Xbox 360 wireless control) and the gameplay is tasty, varied and fun. Important to say that the game brings some interesting novelties to the series as the burst beam that is quite powerful, but consumes a lot of energy (the predecessor game in the series, "G-Darius", had a similar beam but with a different activation method) and also the possibility of burst beam detach out of the ship and can be rotated, served not only to destroy enemies, but also as an interesting temporary shield. Another new feature is an multiplicative score combo system which makes a huge difference in the scores when used wisely. "Dariusburst CS" also brings a good availability of ships which originally comes inside the game, with some new and also classic ships, coming from previous games in the serie, jeeping the same characteristics of their armaments, this fact gives a beautiful touch of nostalgia to the game. The soundtrack is one of the strongest aspects of this title, presenting quality compositions, including vocal and also classic remixed soundtracks of the series, another nice touch of nostalgia. "Dariusburst CS" is an amazing  shoot'em up of modern times and no doubt an excellent addition to the classic and iconic Darius series, bringing a lot of interesting content that entertains for a long time. short mode: Darius is a horizontal shootemup where enemies are giant fishes.  This game features over a dozen of different ships to choose from and literally thousands of missions to complete.  If you like shump classics such as Gradius and Rtype get this right away.  If you like CAVE style bullet hell style shooters you will appreciate this game as well.  If you are remotely interested in shootemups (shumps) you should get this game.
TLDR mode:
I am a big shump fan and have been playing Darius series from the SNES to Staurn to PS to iPad, and now this on PC. This game basically takes the ships and bosses from all previous games from different platforms and allows you to play with updated graphics on the PC.  It's easy to see how the game has evolved since the earlier days which you basically hold down both bombs and auto fire buttons.  The bomb mechancism from the Gaiden days have been replaced by the Burst mechancism to keep the game fresh.  This game has both depending on the ship you choose. In fact, I think the only game mechanism missing from the previous games is the poke-ball like feature from th G-Darius games.
Speaking of gameplay I would say that this game has the most amount of content you can get from a space shooter.  The CS mode of this game allows you to play missions after missions with different pre-set conditions and ships.  In this mode you can also use your scored points to buy and use other ships from the Darius series.  The other mode of the game you get to play on a very wide screen with up to 4 players straight through the traditional stages.
One of the other things which attracted me to most games is the music.  This game has music samples from all previous Darius series, including the beloved/weird music from the Saturn game.  This ZUNATA group is just good at making shooter game music.
If you lie shumpss just buy this game already, you won't regret it.

It's about time I write a review, I purchased this game a few years back when it was pretty new, and I for the many hours I have played, its been so much fun, and after the recent update, the game is even better, with a new map, West Coast USA, and it's pretty large, and very versatile, the game gets closer and closer to leaving early access every day and becomes more polished. The game is easily worth the price tag, and ensures many hours of fun, you can literally edit anything you want, even use the map editor for more adjustment and if you want to, make your own mods, maps, or whatever! The game does have some issues however, that I will list below:
Issues
- The UI is quiet frankly really really laggy in many cases, which is unfortunate as it ties into core gameplay, such as editing vehicles, adding vehicles, switching maps, tuning etc. I really think they should focus on UI and UX, more than many things at the moment, as it's so important to get that right, maybe make the UI more modern, something like Forza UI, or the new NFS payback UI, it would really enhance the game, and gameplay.
- The performance is obviously not perfect, in fact it's not bad, however there is room for improvement, without a shadow of doubt. The actual graphics performance is great, no issues there, however when it comes down to CPU load, and latency, thats where the issues are, especially with large maps for example, im not sure how they handle LODs, but I think it needs to be adressed, as it seems to be the main issue on CPU load. Of course, the cars are also heavy on the CPU, maybe look into the physics optimization, obviously this is not easy, it's a custom physics system and would be very hard to adjust quickly, not only does the cars physics hit perf, but the more cars, the performance drops exponentially, which is unfortunate as it would be nice to see AI (especially on west coast), as it would call for more real crashes etc.
- The physics, while they are very good, they are not perfect, in some cases, the car stretches, in the real world, metal stretches, until it tears apart, I believe panel tearing would be a very good addition, furthermore the cars can also be too soft, and theres singnificant bounces to body work as it hits something, almost elastic, this could definitely be more rigid, and act more realistically, in real life a car typically act rigid when it hits something, and there is little bounce. I also think that they should add material properties to seperate objects, such as wood in the interior would not bend, it would pop out, or snap, for example, this could work with the body tearing idea, potentially adding different amount of tearing based on material! Dashboards should also not bend, but should snap, and pop out like IRL, it would be amazing if this is possible!
- The decals, particles etc. I think that when you crash, there should be fluid spills, coolant, oil, water etc. and lots of persistent particles should fly out, like a real life crash, gears and plastic scattered everywhere, with collisions, it would add a huge amount of realism! I also think they need dirt sprayed onto the car, when you go through mud, or a dirt road! that would be very nice to see, and add scratches for when you brush on something.
- The graphics, I think the graphics are alright, 'meh' in many ways, I do find it unfortunate that the Torque 3D engine is being used, I dont want to hate the engine, but its capabilities are limited, and so is performance, maybe it was down to licensing or whatever, but a different game engine may of suited better, I understand the devs used Cryengine before, I believe that they should of stuck with that, they are too far in now anyway to even consider anything like an engine, but just a thought, mainly towards graphics capabilities. Can Torque 3D handle PBR?
Despite the issue the game is great, the devs are doing a great job and I thank them very much for that! I rate the game overall at 8.8/10 its very good, but needs some more work (many basic things are overlooked). :)

There are no complicated controls and functions that serve very little purpose(At least from my experience - this might differ for someone else) and has an adequate story for the price. There are very clearly defined character roles throughout, which I personally thought were well written and served a purpose.
My only complaint is the lack of control over the 'drift' of your ship and maneuverability, which often results in you crashing into a frigate, something which can result in your instant death depending on the ship you are piloting and the speed you are going at.
Overall, though i've not played much of it so far, I would highly recommend this, especially at the sale price(69p at my time of writing - 02/08/17). Two things right off the bat; I'm not going to get into all of the matchmaking and leveling up issues that plagued this game at release. That stuff has been ironed out, and in my opinion is no longer relevant. Second, I pretty much never play online multiplayer, so this has been a very unique experience for me. Being a horror fan, however, I was immediately interested in this game from the time I first found out about it. I was thinking of waiting to buy it until the campaign and AI features were added, but decided to pull the trigger after watching some gameplay videos. I have been hooked, to say the least. The asymmetrical multiplayer works really well for a game like this, and aside from a few unfortunate exceptions, the other people playing are usually cooperative and quite entertaining. Once you find a character you like and figure out their nuances and how to use them to your advantage, you can become pretty competitive playing as a counselor. I went from dying every round to surviving at least half the time fairly quickly. As for playing as Jason, it's awesome as expected. As with counselors, each version of Jason has his own strengths and weaknesses, but it's pretty hard to go wrong. If you use your abilities effectively, you'll be successful. I am still looking forward to the single player features, since it will offer the chance to play as Jason whenever I feel like it, but I can honestly say that I already consider this money very well spent.

This is one of those games that should be in "Meh" category... It is not bad enough to be "Not Recommended", neither is it good enough to be in the better of the two...
Keep in mind, that I did not play the first part, and just read the story on the webz... It might, or might not have influenced my opinion on the game.
So, short review... This game is a classic shooter, no-brainer, in which you usually just need to run around and kill large quantities of enemies. Story is short and okayish, and the game would probably be worse if it dragged for more than those couple of hours, and for those who like it, there is New Game +...
Gun play is fine, but nothing special, and it bothered me that I usually didn't know what gun I used (it was not really important), as long as I had enough ammunition for any of those...
Blood and gore are all around, and if you are not okay with it, don't play this game...
Experience system is somewhat important at the beginning, but later on, I just didn't know what perks to buy (they are all nothing special), so finished the game with many unspent points...
Graphics is ok, but, as the name of the game suggests, too dark :)
Final verdict is "Meh"... It is ok game for a few hours of no-brainer fun, but nothing more than that... On the other hand, I don't like these kind of shooters to much, so it might be only me :)

I enjoyed playing Half-Life 2 alone before Synergy came along and it goes without saying that Synergy makes is an added-value for no price. The very beginning showed that HL2 could potentially have a co-op feature and this add-on solves it all. This is an essential modification for HL2/EP owners and it definitely renews the game for a little while longer.
I understand this is server-side, but the server could use a bit of work. A prime example would be when the first map, the train station map, is completed. I would find servers newly made to have a problem where it crashes. It may not happen to everyone, but some server administrators, like myself, can get frustrated off that. It's also a little bit of a bother that a Synergy server cannot be officially run from a Linux server, so that's a little bit of a downside.
Otherwise, if you own HL2/EPs, get this add-on. It's definitely one to have for when you want to do more after completing the story or when you want to complete the story with others cooperatively!

This just might be my favorite FPS of all time. There is decent gun variety, and the gunplay is fluent, but who cares? YOU HAVE TWO DEMON ARMS. One can grab objects (and people) to use as weapons, and the other can be used to slash your enemies to pieces. You know what that means? Quad wielding. Now you may be thinking to yourself: "Man, this game looks like a huge power trip." And you're half right. On the easier difficulties, you feel like a god. But on the harder difficulties, its a whole other story. Not to mention the lights. You grow weaker in the light, and cannot use your demon arms. But luckily for you, you have guns to shoot these lights with. Or, if you want to conserve ammo, you can throw stuff at them or slash them. There is a tech tree that branches 4 ways, with no one branch feeling useless. There are also relics that you can collect, each one with a cool backstory. This is one of the only games where I actually care about getting all the collectibles. Multiplayer is there too, but I wouldn't bother. No one plays it, and without people to play with, its just boring. The point is, I love this game, and you should too.

I played this game passionately - have a look at my playtime. Me and my friends went through very good and bad times, went throughout heights and depths, I went through love and hate for myself and my opponents. The atmosphere and idea of this game is great and unique. In my opinion the base game uniqueness is absolutely unrivaled.
But there is one flaw, an essential one for a survival game: Cheaters. Nether was infested from the beginning of my era and it only has gotten worse and worse. There never was and still not is any effective cheat detection or protection in this game.
A game that could be extremely addictive and fun, intense solo or with friends, able to pull out the most multifarious feelings out of your synapses - suddenly turns into the complete opposite.
For me as a “veteran” of Nether it feels like the developers were parents that gave their own beloved child heroin as a 13th birthday present and then sitting down and watch it passing away.

Personally, I love the game. It has, in my opinion, a very rewarding combat system, if you win. Seriously though, Ubisoft. FIX YOUR DAMNED SERVERS! Dont make a good game that no-one can play cos they cant connect to the bloody thing!

I had the pleasure to play and finish the Darkness II and I was pleasantly surprised by how entertaining this game was.
I have never played the first Darkness game, so I thought I would find myself lost; however, this game has a nice recap that puts you up to date from the get go.  I found the story telling very interesting, intriguing, and captivating.  I always wanted to know what would happen to Jackie Estacado, his family, friends, and loved ones.
The gameplay is a mixture between FPS and role playing game (Skyrimish when it comes to the Darkness skills).  I think it's a great combination, and I hope that they would emphasize the role playing aspect more in future games.  I strongly believe that this franchise has the potential to make way more money if they shift the balance from FPS with a little RPG elements, to RPG with FPS elements.  Especially that the story telling is pretty good!  Additional quests/subquests would make it more appealing to a larger audience in my humble opinion.
I had a great time playing this game and I would recommend it to anyone who wants to explore the Darkness universe.  Finally, I would like to thanks the developers for making this game, and I hope to see more coming from you guys! :)
Verdict: B+

SOMA is one of the most thought-provoking story-driven games I have ever played. The story itself is constructed very well and makes you wonder things about not only the game itself, but it even taps into reality as a human being.
The baseline of this game is that you are thrown into a post-apocalyptic world as some confused and terrified character named Simon, who simply went into the doctor's office for a brain scan; and something went wrong, naturally. You then traverse through the dangerous environment deep below the Atlantic, searching for answers as to what is going on in this hellish world. The fact that Simon is in just about the same position as you, the player, being clueless and feeling vulnerable, makes it all the more immersive. The rest of the story, I'd have to leave up to you to find out about, as most of this game is purely about figuring out what's going on in the PATHOS-II Facility.
The gameplay itself is very basic, where you only do a few things to interact with the environment. You can open/close doors, use your handy tool to unlock stuff, find banks of information to learn more about the world and what happened at PATHOS-II, and run in terror from horribly frightening monsters. The monsters, at their cores, are quite similar in that they will chase you down until you die, but I love the diversity of them. Once again I don't want to spoil much about them, but there are monsters which you'd rather see as opposed to another... The only way you can evade death from those frightening and corrupted creatures is by hiding, running, or outsmarting them. You get no weapons, no means of harming them, nothing, it's up to you to get out of the way of danger; that alone makes the game terrifying.
Overall, the atmosphere is incredibly immersive with its excellent sound and visual design. I only encountered about one visual bug throughout the entire game, but even then you'd have to basically search for that bug. The monsters sound creepy as hell, the eerie ambient noises of being deep below the surface in a deteriorating facility make you paranoid as all hell, and the sea life makes you want to never venture below the waves again, and just get back into that horribly claustrophobic monster-infested facility.
Pros
Cons
tl;dr This game is a masterpiece, and if you are into Sci-fi, you need this game. While it is a linear story and you don't get very many other things to do after you've completed the campaign, the story itself makes that worth the price for me, but may be pricy to others. As a bonus, there is fully functioning workshop capabilities where you can make your own stories, and play others'.
If you're into horror, it's a must-buy while it's on sale.

A fantastic example of a horror game that actually goes beyond what many smaller studios think is necessary of a horror game. Instead of relying on tired gameplay and tropes -- oh it's a dark house, and I only have a flashlight -- Soma explores something deeper, namely consciousness and the grey area that exists implanting human consciousness in artificial, man made technology. Set in an underwater compound, after a catastrophe that has potentially wiped out life on the surface, you're set with a task of preserving humanity however you can, in whatever medium possible.
Following up from Amnesia: Dark Descent, a solid game that saw a lot of attention and hype despite being fairly by-the-numbers was always going to be somewhat of a difficult task, but Soma succeeds by pushing out of that comfort zone and trying something brave and something new. Something that genuinely elicits thought.
All in all, an enthralling idea, world and concept, but widely similar gameplay to its predecessor. A very necessary purchase for any horror fan.

I don't often review games, but I had to for this one. This is an awesome little game that is clearly a labor of love. If you don't mind the small concessions to the console gaming (fiddly controls in particular) then you'll find a surprisingly deep tactical strategy game that is authentically steeped in BSG lore. The campaign can be challenging and unpredictable as it mixes predictable story missions with a dynamic X-Com-ish strategy layer where you have to fight off cylon raids and keep the colonies together.
Unlike many strategy games there is real depth here in the combat. You can play around with many different tactics and there are uses for every loadout and ship. For example in the early game you might want to use your manticore corvettes as frontline tanks to keep the enemy off your frigates, while in the late-game you might load them out with nukes and use them to blast through enemy formations at high-speed scouting their ships and taking a few out before your battlestars and carriers get into the mix.
This game really is a gem. There's some rough edges, but they're worth it. Easily my favorite game of the year.

This is a "meh" strategy game and a fantastic tactics game.
Strategic Layer:
The strategic layer (that is, the map of the 12 colonies that you play over for the campaign) is a little bland and clunky. It works pretty well when you only have a few fleets wandering around, but once you have a dozen or more, plus groups flying around to replace losses or rebalance fleets, it shows its limitations. It's extremely simple - defending the colonies from Cylons keeps them happy, and happy colonies keep paying you to defend them. The mobile construction yard that you build ships out of is a fun little conceit, but I found myself leaving it in one place after the first few missions of the campaign.
Tactical Layer:
The tactical layer is extremely fun, and is the game's strong point. It's enjoyable to play around with all of the different ships, manuver them, try to make the best out of the strength and weaknesses of each class. This, incidentally, is why I think if you're going to buy the game, you should buy the DLC. A couple of extra ship classes may not seem like a huge deal, but the different ship classes and how you can use them in tactical combat are really the "meat" of the game's content. A handful of extra tactical options for 5 bucks is well worth it, in my opinion, as this is where the game's fun lies.
Each fleet is limited to seven ships, so there are no "throwaway" units - once your fleet is deployed for battle, each of your units is important and you have to get the most out of them. This is a refreshing change of pace, contrasting with so many strategy games that involve masses of fodder on both sides. In Deadlock, when you lose a ship in a battle, just a single ship, it often really is an "oh ****" moment.
My only real gripe on the tactical side is that you can't roll ships - it's annoying that if one of your ships loses armor on a side, you have to turn it instead of rolling to present an undamaged aspect.
Other/Concluding Throughts:
The game's biggest weakness is a lack of replayability. Though I enjoyed it, I found myself with no desire to play the campaign again once I played through it once. Some additional campaign missions to extend the expereince could bring me back to it. I may play skirmish mode here and there in the future, but unless there is story DLC or a major campaign update I don't think I'm likely to put a ton more time into this game.
Unfortunately, multiplayer seems dead. However if you can talk some friends into getting the game too, you can probably get some more play out of it buy squaring off against them in multiplayer.
Still, it was a fun game, and by playing the campaign very slowly (I did tons of side missions and other battles, only doing a main mission infrequently) I got 23 hours out of it. Not bad for $40 of game plus $5 of DLC in my mind.

Evil Genius: “It’s good to be bad.” And it certainly is; Evil Genius gives you the player the ability to be, well, an evil genius, bent on world domination! Take control of your choice of three evil geniuses and run you’re evil underground lair complete with expendable minions, gloriously crazy henchmen, a storeroom full of gold and treasures from around the world and a path to world domination. A solid game in its own right, Evil Genius harkens to the likes of the beloved Dungeon Keeper games or more recent games like Impire or, War of the Overworld. You must protect your evil genius as you complete objectives and running an evil lair, ordering acts of infamy upon the unsuspecting world and taking steps to completely ruling the world. You take an isometric view of the game and task minions to build rooms inside of a mountain, the rooms all with different purposes to aid you in your goals. The game is simple to get the hang of with a very comprehensive tutorial and laid back pace, you won’t be stressing out over anything going on as you attempt to conquer the world. Some gameplay design choices are odd and prohibit some of the games systems (such as building traps) to be near useless or too costly to use over other strategies. The game is also victim to going on too long before starting to feel too repetitive and easy. The style of the game feels very much like a comic book, lots of colors and stylized characters and minions. Music and sound are both low-key, music during gameplay is on the same song and same loop, it won’t really grab your attention and is decent ambiance, and the sounds of the various rooms are also low key with little beeps and boops, you have to zoom in fairly close to actually hear them.  The music while sitting on the main menu screen is very jazzy and awesome and, can easily make you feel like you already own the world, they just don’t know it yet. Overall, Evil Genius is a solid strategy and base simulator, if you even are remotely interested or loved the aforementioned Dungeon Keeper games, I highly recommend dropping the $10.00 USD and buying it for yourself, I also see it go on sale only during the major Steam sales for less than a couple of cheeseburgers at McDonalds so if you’re money is tight wait to pick it up and be sure you do, otherwise you’ll be waiting a while before another sale.
-Thumbs Up from Royial

dream and
game. They don't go to a cubicle day after day and get paid to develop this game. They likely have jobs outside of this game just to pay bills and they develop this in their free time.

When you buy this you are in no way entitled to tell them to do anything, how to do it, when to do it, or what to do. You have 0 entitlement in this game just like in any other. Buying this is a contribution from you to them saying, "Hey, I'm here to help you with your dream, because it's mine too."

Overall, most of these negative reviews can be picked apart for the BS they are. I'm not biased towards this game and it has its issues but I highly respect these developers for their free time into this game they want to make not only for themselves but for the community that loves it.

Ever since I saw Dariusburst AC's arcade cabinet, I knew. With a play area covering two widescreen TVs, Dariusburst AC was impressive before you even sat down. This is lost somewhat in the conversion - the PC edition allows you to use multiple monitors, but most people won't go through the trouble (myself included). Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours is an enhanced port of Dariusburst AC (which itself was a widely expanded reimagining of a PSP game of the same name).
The arcade content is exactly as it was in the arcade - you have eight ships to choose from, and several routes to take. Scoring revolves around two mechanics - building a multiplier by killing enemies and not getting hit, and using your ship's "burst" function for an extra multiplier on top of that. Ships will have different bursts and different multiplier rates, which means scoring with each ship means learning to approach the game very differently with different ships. It's rather simple, but very deep and very satisfying. From a score play perspective, Dariusburst is the best Darius has ever been. The arcade mode is entirely accurate, which means the original 32:9 aspect ratio is maintained and shrunk to fit. If your monitor isn't big enough, you may find things too small for your tastes. Which is where Chronicle mode comes in.
Chronicle mode uses the same basic system, but is resdesigned for a standard 16:9 display. The game structure is also different - instead of choosing your path through three stages, you select areas on a map that contain preset levels (not limited to 3!) and an assigned ship. There are dozens of these areas, and some of them are extremely long and difficult if you play on the default settings. It's a mildly enjoyable distraction from the arcade game, but it's so expansive that you're not likely to devote time to refining your play on any area and therefore stands more as a survival-focused companion to the main game.
Musically Dariusburst is fantastic, with expertly crafted tracks synchronised to the action (in the arcade mode, anyway). The visual design  is a step back from Darius Gaiden and G.Darius. It's all very competent, but none of the environments are memorable. Several of the bosses - Great Thing is the obvious example - are impressive, but that's largely a matter of scale and effective scripting of the battles. Neither screenshots nor videos adequetely communicate just how fantastic the game design is.
The DLC ships are a lot of fun to use, but they're tragically sandboxed in their own little mode - very similar to Chronicle mode, but laid out in menu format and with no progression aspect. In that respect it's disappointing - much as I love the arcade mode's perfect accuracy, I think I would love the opportunity to play Dariusburst AC meets Fantasy Zone more. Modding community, where are you?
Overall, Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours is currently the best shmup on Steam. There's a lot of content for those who need boxes to tick, and there's depth for those who like to perfect their execution in well-crafted challenges. The eight unique ships add a great deal of variety, and just learning what makes each of them work is enjoyable in itself. I can't reccomend Dariusburst enough.

It's an okay game, but it has issues, which is why I've refrained from rating it either way so far. However, I'm down-voting it now because I've seen too many valid threads (notably some with suggestions, which took time to write) just vanish from the forums where they could at least just have been locked rather than destroyed plain and simple. If you're going to censor, at least assume it instead of concealing it like sneaky *****.
That being said, on with the issues:
- no solo mode (we were promised a solo mode as a justification for the release being postponed for half a year)
- the game has a "party" feature, where friends can join a public match together. That's very fine. However, that party feature allows party members to become killer, meaning we often see a killer who is friend with some survivors, and who actually behaves friendly with them, focusing on killing the few other survivors who are not his friends. Sometimes even with the assistance of the survivors who are his friends. That's totally messed up and ruins games. It's also quite a common occurrence.
- some achievements are broken
- there are quite a few exploits, most notably one that allows people to edit other people's accounts (destroying their perks), and also others that allow survivors to become unreachable to the killer
- the perks are unlocked randomly, and you don't have enough space to own one of each perk (apparently there are 40 types or perks but you only have 30 spaces), so you'll have to sell perks without any reliable way of earning them back later
- the game has a voicechat, which is nice and nicely incorporated (the distance matters, or you can find walkie-talkies to communicate long distance), but it lacks a text chat alternative for people without a microphone. Or better yet, pre-recorded voice messages (think Wolfenstein Enemy Territory or UT99)

This is a very strange game, that I personally love, but I'll admit it's not for everyone.  It has some very unique artistic and musical sensibilities, and even its game design is pretty far outside the norm for shoot'em ups.  The game actually gets easier the more times you replay, because you earn points to unlock things like extra starting lives. Everyday Shooter is the definition of a cerebral experience. Stunning, almost overwhelming visuals and the melodies bring the utmost life to this abstract 2D shooter.
The progression is solid, but can be somewhat confusing as to what each of the elements represents. You'll find the mechanics switching between tunes and having to re-learn what mechanics are important for that song. Once you master this understanding and adapatability, you'll quick enjoy moving song to song.
The actual gameplay mechanics are decent, but you'll often struggle with just the intensity of visuals happening at once. Similiar to titles like Geometry Wars, you'll be placed into the full color spectrum of insanity quite quickly. Fear not though, again once you grasp the "rules" for that specific song, you'll like fair ok.
My biggest complain on the tunes I played was not having the "Clear All" mechanic found in bullet hell games. It certainly would have saved me in a few areas. The controls responded well and I was able to competently play without much struggle.
If you're into abstract/cerebral games, Everyday Shooter is one to pick up.

This game had a server in our country back then, titled Dragonica. To see this game still alive despite the challenge of time, I believe the game has the great feat. Sure, parts of my review may be biased due to nostalgia, but I still think this game is awesome. To summarize this game, Dragon Saga is your typical MMORPG with the Warrior, Mage, Archer, and Thief. It is a 2D side-scrolling game with an adjustable view. Graphics-wise, it is player-friendly, acceptable to the eyes of both the young and the old; gameplay-wise, it is fine, quick and fitting for an MMORPG genre. The community's population seems to be average, if not low, but with that player base, I believe the game can still hold on longer. Like any other MMORPGs, the flaw of this game is still connected to the gaming term "Pay-to-Win" (P2W).
This is one of the three MMORPGs I grew up with, with Grand Chase and Dragon Nest as the other two. MMORPGs teach players most of the gaming lessons, as the genre is versatile and flexible. I assure you, that if you played games like this, under the genre I specified on the previous premise, you can adjust to any other game genre just fine.
That's all I would say, for now. Enjoy gaming!

I would love to recommend this game. I personally found this game really fun... when I had the time to dedicate to playing it.
The developers have the right to design what they want, and prioritise what they want. From time to time, these developments fall in line with what players suggest, ask for or point out would be useful. Other times, they seem to be a thousand miles off base. But arguably the worst part, I find, is the attitude I've seen. There is an attitude of entitlement that feels unnecessarily aggressive, and in turn it's bred a horrible attitude throughout the player base too, making this one of the most divisive games I've ever seen.
And that is why I can't recommend this game.
I can't in good conscience recommend a game that has the sandbox mode removed, and when people ask for it to return (because not all of us can work at home and dedicate several hours every day to progress just one or two dinosaur stages, only to wind up losing it every time servers need to reset or every time that we die) there is an overtone of threat from the developers themselves. "Shut up or it's never coming back." This, in turn, then leads the playerbase to be equally split - those who continue to point out that we genuinely don't have time for such an extreme progression system but love the survival aspect of the game and genuinely would love to play - and those who tell people to effectively sod off and find a different game if they don't like the survival system.
Here's the thing: I love the survival aspect of this game. I adore it. I want to love the notion of a progression system. But it has been made incredibly obvious that the progression system will never work out for me, with my time schedule. I won't ever reach a top tier dinosaur (not that I particularly want to, to be honest) and I'll be lucky to enjoy mid-tier dinosaurs for any length of time. And to clarify: I've never asked for the sandbox to come back, and I appreciate that the devs need people to play the progression system so they can test it.
But the attitude of the developers, and in turn the attitude it has bred in players, is ultimately what seals my non-recommendation for me. I can't recommend a game where the developing team behind it has an attitude of "Sod off" and they let that same attitude run rampant in their playerbase, because then they don't have to look like the guilty party by saying it themselves any more. I don't want to recommend a game where it's so easy to die and lose the progression you work hard for because important systems - like a scent system to help guide players to water in maps where there are no landmarks - and people will write off your critique of the system as you being some "carebear baby who can't play survival" when the reality is that, mechanically, the game is lacking and the odds stacked against you.
I want to recommend this game. I want to be able to change this review one day and say that the proper mechanics exist, that the progression system isn't so utterly poor because of several other missing mechanics that make survival so hard. I want to be able to say that the developers listen, take suggestions and regard feedback with a level head. Maybe one day, I'll be able to. But right now, I certainly can't, and as much as I want to love Isle, I can't recommend it to any who would be interested in purchasing it. Unless you enjoy grinds more frustrating than Korean MMOs that take just as long - except with the added bonus of losing all the progress you ever made.

Ignored by most western gamers, beloved by a niche & reviled by others, the Darius series has always been a bizarre one... in more ways than one. Mechanically, it's in a specific place between "mainstream shmup everyone and their grandmothers has played" and "turbo-hardcore bullet-curtain bonanza where the projectiles are many, the screen is busy and the ships are all piloted by girls or guys that all embody a specific anime fetish". Darius is accessible enough that the everyman may happen to give it a shot, but maybe not inaccessible enough for some members of the hardcore shmup community. As a result, you'll find that even the most beloved older entries in this series get reviews that complain about them being "too tough" or "unfair", despite the difficulty being much more beginner-friendly than the average Cave game.
This is largely because Darius, unlike many other shooters of its kind where one hit means death, has an upgradable shield system; that way, the difficulty ramps up to crazy levels, but even low-level players can feel like they can achieve things. In that regard, this game's the best in the series; while not "hand-holding", both Arcade and Chronicle Saviours modes put effort into guiding you towards high-level play, not through tutorials but through masterfully executed pacing. The first few CS missions, anyone could beat but it will just keep ramping up more and more, until you're fighting screen-filling monstrosities with barely any health. This format, however, is a double-edged sword; on one hand, CS mode's length creates a perfect learning curve. On the other hand, it sometimes loses the adventurous, over-the-top feeling of playing Gaiden or G; level assets and base designs for bosses are often blatantly recycled. The levels can feel like they were created (extremely well, but still) with a level creator and you will find yourself playing increasingly difficult versions of what is basically the same stage. Even including the recycling, though, DBCS still has far more content AND more solid, player-friendly mechanics than many of its rival shmups (I'm looking at you, Ikaruga stage 2) that I don't feel the price is hugely unwarranted. I paid 35 for it, and chances are it'll go down for good as time goes on; if the game grabs you in a particular way or if you're a really hardcore scrolling shmup fan, the price shouldn't bother you. Otherwise wait for a sale. I recommend checking out the second Taito arcade game collection on PS2; it has both Gaiden and G in it. My main reason for purchasing this was to support the series for what it represents as a whole moreso than to own this specific game.
The bosses have more specific, memorable patterns than ones found in more Cave-inspired games, where the bosses can kind of mesh together. I don't remember specific bullet patterns in Crimzon Clover that well, but the attacks of the Stare or Fossil-types in Darius will always stay with me.
The biggest difference between my view and that of the gaming mainstream lies in what many believe to add to a game's "content" or its "bang for their buck"; I don't really care if I can watch Flash cartoons on TV, watch real-life stand-up comic acts and be immersed in a "living, breathing world"; I don't need the oh-so-important "quiet time" and "pacing" of pushing a block onto a switch. I just want a game with non-stop, carefully-crafted, solid mechanics and design and DBCS does a great job at that. Those that think shmups are "easy to make" and thus should be ten bucks by default simply haven't thought deeply about what goes into a well-crafted game.
An issue I didn't have while playing normally, yet couldn't help but notice when recording footage for a video review, is the lack of a replay feature. Other nitpicks that some players found game-breaking are the lack of practice options for stages, no English translation for the arcade mode loading screens, no online multiplayer and no option to change the color of the ships without multiple controllers (yep, this is getting REALLY straw-grasping at this point). One legit issue is the lack of ship-capturing, which was a really cool element from G and Gaiden, and yet another extremely minor nitpick is that the Dragonball Z-esque beam war animation of the G-style ships, while still pretty freaking badass, is not quite quite as cool-looking as its original variant.
You get many different ships from all throughout the history of the series that allow for various play styles, either a little different or radically different depending on the type of burst shot or bomb attack, or whether you even have a burst shot or bomb attack at all - the ships from the first two games are the hardest to use because you only have basic fire & missiles. A slightly annoying element is that the controls for the placement of your burst turret can be inverted depending on the ship you're using, which makes for an extra element you have to pay attention towards that wasn't really needed.
The art direction beyond the boss designs is possibly my biggest issue; the levels, while still full of enemies flying around in beautifully planned out routes like mechanical shoals, look pretty bland compared to the sheer beauty of G and Gaiden's settings. The bosses make up for this, though, being well-designed by famous anime mecha designers with the foresight of a stylishly blocky aesthetic not held back by hardware limitations (remember that Darius Burst started as a PSP game).
Graphically, it's worth pointing out the two-monitor & widescreen set-up that this game allows, along with the visual downgrade of arcade mode that you'll experience otherwise. It's a port of the Dariusburst you'll experience in arcades, thus you'll get a minimized, inferior version if you're playing on one, non-widescreen monitor - the same issue you have when playing the original game on an emulator. Nonetheless I didn't find this to be game-breaking at all and I still find arcade mode engaging.
A common issue people have with this series is its music. From its very beginnings back in 1986, if you reached the iconically-designed, Go Nagai-esque King Fossil in the original Darius, your battle was accompanied by a melody that just... didn't sound quite right. For nearly three decades this tradition has been kept, this very game being heavily marketed using the level theme of the beginning of its Chronicle Saviours mode: a jazzy track with vocals that just feel... a tad off. This is because, from the get-go, Darius set out to create its own unique identity among the flood of shoot-em-ups of its era; a STRANGE identity. Surreal visuals, bizarre music written to inspire a variety of emotions; from relaxation, to getting high off your♥♥♥♥♥ to a psychotic fit; and, above all else, a marine theme and a difficulty to match that make you feel like you are mere bait in a massive space-ecosystem of mechanical sea life. It's a type of game with genuine artistic merit that is never acknowledged as such.
Just as Darius Gaiden, back in 1994, had its soundtrack panned by game magazines of the time ("[like] some fat bint warbling away like an Old Spice advert" so does Chronicle Saviours' most popular English upload have a comment section flooded with "wtf is this garbage music" comments. The gaming community doesn't seem very accepting of music that gets across emotions that go beyond what is typical, but the bizarre nature of Zuntata's music for Darius is obviously not a result of incompetent songwrighting; the falsettos have their carefully-controlled purpose. It's not Trout Mask Replica-level, but it still helps contribute hugely to this series' sense of identity.
So, long story short; a unique and fun game, part of a fun and unique series. If you're not quite sure if this is your thing, try Gaiden and G first and see what impact they have on you and if you think it's too expensive, just wait until the next sale.

My experience playing the game is decent, I've had my share of thrills and disappointments but thats to be expected from a early access game. I'm going to say right off the bat that if you're buying this game expecting to play you're favorite Dinosaur right off the rip then you're better off saving you're money because thats not possible without hard work earning them.
People also seem to ignore the store page when it says its in early access and get upset when they are met with problems. The Isle changes frequently which brings good and bad things with it, be patient and let the Devs iron out these problems and make changes accordingly.
I'm going to start my review by telling you about the game.
Graphics: The game is beautifully designed with a stunning/immersive environment were the entire map can be used in you're favor or be just as dangerous as the creatures roaming through it. There will be many Biomes to explore to you're liking with different sights and secrets to find.
Playable options: There will be a wide variety of creatures to choose from. Dinosaurs, Soldiers, Tribals and Cannibals, all amazingly detailed and animated. This game will have the largest selection of playables I've seen and I'm really looking forward to it. (Soldiers, Tribals, and Cannibals aren't in the game yet.)
Gamestyle: There is but one game mod being worked on and thats Progression, were it will take all of you're wits to make it through. Start off as a defensless creature and work you're way up the food chain, mistakes can be punishing. If you don't got the patience to try agian then the game isn't for you. It can be frustrating at times but its all apart of the experience of becoming better at the game, you've been warned on the store page that this game won't be a walk in the park for you.
Development: The game has some very dedicated Devs that works on The Isle frequently to keep the game moving forward.
I'm going to bring up some things players might experience on this game that might help give people a forewarning.
System requirement: Since this game has so much detail and work put into it. This does a number on low end computers, You might struggle to run The Isle so I'd advice either buying a new PC or playing the game on lowest settings possible. Or just wait until there is more options to adjust the game settings.
One of the most noticable problems I've had with the game is netcoding, which causes lagging, freezing, rubberbanding and even crashing on some occasions. I think the devs should seriously look into this because it makes playing the game very difficult.
Devs: Something that is always being fused about, I'm just going to give my honost opinion here. The devs aren't the nicest people you'll meet, they can be rude and insensitive, some times its uncalled for, and other times it is because people seem to act like entitled kids and complain about things thats already being worked on or subjected to change. People need to learn to be patient with early accessed games, nothing can be handed to you immediately, It takes time for things to be developed and tweaked to satisfying standards. And the whole point of a EARLY ACCESS game is for things to be changed, if you can't accept changes made to the game then The Isle isn't for you.
This game CAN be fun, Its probably one of the most intense surivival game I've played. People that compain about it being boring is missing the entire point, what do you expect to do as a animal? animals don't do much but survive and get by on the skin of their teeth. You're best bet is to wait for humans if you're easily bored.
So all in all the game is very promising and I'd like to see how it comes along in the future. I recommend it to people that have the patience to put up with issues and the current game mode, If not then save you're money, choice is you'rs. I'll come along and change this review when I come up with more to say.

I have a very funny story to tell about this 28 MB download
It all started when we got a new refridgerator with a neat little color screen and a keypad
as soon as the warranty ran out, the refridgeration unit broke
we tried to get it fixed to no avail
My wife wanted to throw it out, but when I was checking out the electronics I noticed it had an ARM chip on a board with what appeared to be some non-volatile flash memory, and some on-board RAM
I had an idea, and decided to keep it
I had read online that some guy had actually ported doom to a toaster, one of those fancy ones with a color screen and a d-pad
I wanted to top that
I found an assembly port of DOOM for ARM chipsets and worked out a way to put it on the flash chip by soldering it into USB stick's PCB
I looked up the chip number for the flash chip and it turned out it was a fairly ordinary flash chip found on a lot of sandisk USB sticks, NAND flash.
I cracked open just about half of all the USB thumb drives I own (over 200) and found out I actually owned one with the same chip in it!
I desoldered the chip from the motherboard inside of the fridge control panel and put it in the thumb drive
I found out... it was already formatted! It was even compatible with the electronics inside of the particular thumb drive I was using (it obeyed ONFi standards)
FAT, 128 MB nand flash chip
anyway so long story short i tinkered with the doom assembly and got it to run on the little arm chip on the fridge, and to display on the screen
The assembly i downloaded also allowed me to save to the chip and interestingly enough the write functionality was enabled, something I did not expect although was probably necessary to allow the fridge to save the ice-maker presets and light-on-open-door setting.
anyway so after getting it all working and running, with controls (but no sound), and I put it back in the fridge's front panel and showed it to my wife
Well she was amazed and very impressed but she really thought DOOM wasn't DOOM without the epic soundtrack
So anyway i managed to figure out how to get the motherboard's ice-maker controls to output analog audio and modified the assembly to map the audio out into the address space of the arm chip. It was software-emulated sound, but it had a few voices and channels and was actually better quality than many PC-speakers back in the day.
I hooked it up to a little speaker and E1M1 was just... oh so satisfying. A bit garbled and grainy but I could hear it, and it was there.
So DOOM was running perfectly.
That's the story!
Please tell your stories of porting DOOM to ridiculous setups, i'd love to hear them!

Dariusburst: Chronicle Saviours is a game that completely took me by surprise until I got an E-mail giving me a 50% coupon for this game, and once I saw it, I immediately had to buy it.
I grew up playing the legendary Shoot-Em-Ups of the SNES and SEGA Genesis era, those being Gradius, R-Type, and of course, Darius Force (And Darius Twin). Later on I went on to play G-Darius and then didn't really touch it again until now.
Any fans of the SHMUP genre should pick this up, and I myself have been trying hard to spread this news around to all of my friends to get it as well. It's a MUST HAVE for your Steam Library. This game features over +3000 stages (no, this is not an exageration), 47 Bosses, and over a dozen ships (5 currently DLC, which are also worth the money!) each with their own characteristics, weapons, and abilities that adds an amazing amount of replay value never before seen in ANY SHMUP game since R-Type Final.
My hope is that with the release of the SEGA SHMUP Franchise ships available, Taito will hopefully gain exclusive rights to include the legendary fighters, the Vic Viper of Gradius fame, and the R-9 Arrowhead of R-Type fame respectively into this game. If they do, this game will earn a perfect 10 in my book.
PROS:
-Great SHMUP Mechanics
-Tight controls
-Fairly leanant difficulty curve so any person can pick up the game and play
-4-Player Co-op offers shared power-up pick ups, which has never been done before
-Great Boss Fights
-+3000 Stages!! Can you beat them all?
-Varied Silver Hawk Ships from the earlier games complete with their weapons and abilities
CONS:
-The Harder Stages (EX Mode) will really test your patience
-4-Player Co-op is only for local play, so make sure to grab extra controllers
-Considering there are 3000 stages, some might start to feel "samey", considering there are 47 bosses spreaded amongst them, and not all of them appear in every Game Mode.
Overall, this game will keep you entertained for hours, and it's a great way to introduce any newcomers into the SHMUP franchise and prepare them for the much harder bullet hell games that are currently for sale on Steam. I highly recommend this as a real Steam Library keeper.
