I bought this game as I find a lot of video games have very common themes, engines and sometimes a lot of recycled graphics. Pyre seemed like someone invented their own sport and wanted to get it out there in the open. In short, the game is new, engaging and fun, but can be a little slow to certain groups. For those that enjoy story-driven games, I'm sure you'll love the fairy tale you're about to enter.
Pyre is definitely a game of it's own. Although it does borrow from sports, it does it with it's own style and spin. The
is smooth and definitely dynamic as it allows players to control different characters with different talents. For example, some players are fast and are able to move swiftly while some of the bigger players can only jump, but do a lot more damage on the field and against the goal (or the Pyre). The general setup is there are two Pyres (or goals) in which the players have to come into contact with. Each player is given a set of characters to choose from; some do more damage while some are based off their special abilities or speed. To start the game, players must race to the center and grab the "ball" before the other team does. Even when the other team has the ball, characters can eliminate one another if they step into a defenders "aura" or circle. The size of the circle depends on upgrades as well as the character. The player will the ball can still jump and throw, but cannot eliminate other players while in possession of the ball. It seems quite the effort has been made to distinguish the characters and give them different playstyles and abilities. If I had to point out a down-side / slow-side to the game is that you can only control 1 character at a time while the other characters are still. Mind you - these characters have a role to play if you use them right; placing these characters in strategic locations will definitely serve your purpose.
The
are definitely worth a mention. They follow an art/realistic-ish cartoon style that definitely suits the premise. It does add a uniqueness to the campaign and the gameplay itself. The attention to details was well done and transition scene to scene/place to place is done quite smoothy. It reminds me of the old flash days except the graphics are much more detailed. Most of the graphics are done in 2D, but you will notice some 3D aspects spread throughout the game. Gameplay graphics are quite fluid - they compliment when players impact one another or impact the Pyre. The
are okay. There isn't a lot of dialogue so get your reading glasses out because you'll need them to follow the story. The characters do talk a bit, but their vocabulary is quite limited. The sounds are neither over the top or below average. They do just enough to add some compliments to the gameplay.
Overall, a decent game in my opinion. I like it for the fact it tried something different and it breaks away from typical indie or AAA games. This game is pervasive in its creativity as it transcends to every aspect of the game (from graphics to gameplay). I would recommend you do your homework before buying this one as it might not be your cup of tea. Then again, you might think this is absolutely awesome.
RATING : 7.15/10

I'm still not sure if I totally like this game or not. I went into a big fan of Bastion and Transistor, and found something unlike wat I was expecting. As a story, I absolutely adore it, and the influence and interaction with the story is well done. The player assuming he role of the Reader doesn't feel out of place. It's the sort of thing where I want to go through a bazzilion different times changing one little thing at a time to see what difference that makes to the story... but, at the same time, I don't have any interest in going through the "game" again. The actual gameplay, the "Dog-soccer" Rites grew on me a little after I rebound a few keys and played with the characters enough to understand what they excelled at. At no point in the game however, did the stars shine and I thought to myself, "OH BOY! Can't wait to dive into a fire 7 times." The gameplay of Dog-soccer was extremely unituitive to me, and I'm positive there are some basic gameplay elements that I just never fully grasped. Passing the orb? Why would I do that!
That being said, this is a story I enjoyed experiencing. Everything about it is beautiful. The visuals and music are gorgeous, and the end of the story... just feels right. It's not the sort of game that wraps everything into a happy finale just to give you a happy ending. It however rewards you for the decisions you've made. It's a thoughtful game, with interesting characters (several of the enemy teams seem rather one-dimensional, but maybe I just didn't engage with them right to get their story), and honestly, the mouse-over world information is basically enough for someone forgetful like me to give the game a thumbs up. It's such a smart design in my opinion. I want to see it in every single game from here on out. That, and a story that, at times, rewards you for losing rather than forcing you to play through it agian. Anyway, if you can bear the weird mini game, this is a story well worth experiencing.
